title: Building interiors keep the exterior window glow instead of DFU's WindowStyle.Disabled (black)
claim: DFU lays out interior models with SetClimate(..., WindowStyle.Disabled) (DaggerfallInterior.cs:473/:517/:1270); Disabled sets EmissionColor black (MaterialReader.cs:934-936). Port: interiorContext.js:120 uploads window masks via uploadRecord (dataPipeline.js:89-91); drawMesh binds them (renderer.js:1578) times the global _windowEmission (renderer.js:1114-1115), which is only ever day/night/fog: main.js:67 boots it 'day'; world.js:3295 / exterior.js:1607 write it only in exterior frames (world.js:3070 modal return exits first); worldModes' interior block (:2779-2796) never calls setWindowEmission; WINDOW_STYLES (windowEmission.js:8-13) has no disabled entry.
consequence: Inside every shop/tavern/house, window glass glows pale blue by day and amber at night where DFU/classic show unlit glass; contradicts the port's own bible (Rendering-Arc R2 note: 'emission stays dark (Disabled)').

title: Dispatcher's Day window style overrides the ?interior scene's documented dark emission
claim: main.js:67 runs renderer.setWindowEmission(windowEmissionRGB(params.get('window') || 'day')) BEFORE routing (the ?interior route is line 68), overwriting the renderer's black boot value (renderer.js:468). interior.js:28-30 documents the DFU law it relies on - 'SetClimate with WindowStyle.Disabled - emission stays dark here by default' - and neither interior.js nor interiorContext.js ever calls setWindowEmission, so 'by default' meant the renderer's boot state, which the dispatcher line defeats. The standalone-scene slice of the previous finding: the port disagrees with its own comment one import away.
consequence: The standalone ?interior dev scene draws climate-swapped window records with a day-blue glow instead of the dark glass the scene header and DFU (MaterialReader.cs:934-936) both specify.

title: ?novideo also skips the audio bootstrap, silencing the classic title/menu music
claim: On the classic-skin path the only pre-menu ensureAudio calls are main.js:164 (inside the '!params.has(novideo)' block at :145) and launcherScene.js:41 (reached only via main.js:127: ?launcher or ShowOptionsAtStart, which the launcher exists to turn off). With ?novideo and ShowOptionsAtStart=False, no AudioContext exists before runMenu: music.playSong needs audio.ctx (music.js:105), created only by audio.ensure (audio.js:85/:108/:121-127), which never runs; the song parks in _pending (music.js:118-124) and every retry hits a null ctx. DFU's enableVideos gates ONLY the VidPlayer push (DaggerfallUI.cs:1711-1713); the title song plays regardless (SetupGameWizard.cs:89/:176).
consequence: A classic-skin player with the launcher off using ?novideo (documented as DFU's enableVideos, main.js:137) gets a silent title screen and menu; the armed 5STRONG.HMI survives into the game and can start over the director's track on the first in-game gesture.

title: Four BEAST_DESIGNS entries quote wrong ENEMY_BASICS level/damage
claim: The design-line convention (orcBody.js:12 'anchored to ENEMY_BASICS, not invented'; test/atronachs.test.js:20 pins its numbers) quotes each enemy's EnemyBasics level/damage, but four beasts.js entries diverge from EnemyBasics.cs: GrizzlyBear port 8/[1,20] (beasts.js:127-128) vs C# Level 4, 1-8 (cs:380-388); SabertoothTiger 10/[1,25] (:149-150) vs 4, 1-10 (:413-421); Spider 3/[1,8] (:216-217) vs 4, 5-15 (:446-450); GiantScorpion 9/[1,20] (:237-238) vs 12, 15-25 (:912-916). The port's combat table characters/enemyBasics.js is correct for all four ids (verified), so only these labels are wrong; BEAST_DESIGNS feeds only paperdollPayload.js beastPacks.
consequence: The voxel editor's stat readout shows wrong level/damage for these four enemies; combat is unaffected because ENEMY_BASICS is correct.

title: Duplicate payload keys make the 'tails were never shipped' fix inert
claim: The single payload object literal (lines 535-565) declares `tail` and `tailCat` twice: the audit-annotated fix at lines 543-545 ('THE TAILS WERE NEVER SHIPPED') builds the argonian tail from ARGONIAN_HIDE, but the same literal re-declares `tail: packPiece(buildTail(ramps.skin,'argonian'))` and `tailCat` at line 565; the later duplicates win under JS object-literal semantics, so the line-544 ARGONIAN_HIDE build is computed and thrown away and the shipped argonian tail pack is colored with the human skin ramp.
consequence: The editor payload's argonian tail mesh ships in human skin tones instead of ARGONIAN_HIDE until the viewer's applyTone recolors it (tools/paperdollViewer.js:617); the fix line is dead code and the two declarations will drift.

title: resolvePaperdollRecord/isCloak have no src caller; law duplicated inline
claim: resolvePaperdollRecord (paperdollArt.js:20-27) and its exported isCloak helper - the file's stated verbatim port of DaggerfallUnityItem.GetInventoryTextureRecord's variant resolution (cs:1740-1764) - have no caller in src/ (grep finds only test/paperdollart.test.js and test/piece.test.js); the live copy of the same record law is re-implemented inline in systems/itemTemplates.js:133-144 with its own private CLOAK_TEMPLATES set (itemTemplates.js:79), so two copies exist and only the inline one runs.
consequence: No player-visible effect today (copies agree), but a fix applied to the exported 'one home' copy - e.g. the C# IsArtifact carve-out at DaggerfallUnityItem.cs:1746-1748, absent from both - would never reach the running path.

title: Wraith design damage [10,45] contradicts EnemyBasics MinDamage 20
claim: undeadBody.js:467 gives the Wraith design 'damage: [10, 45]' in a file whose sibling entries cite ENEMY_BASICS as source (e.g. Zombie :112). DFU EnemyBasics.cs:1016-1017 has Wraith MinDamage = 20, MaxDamage = 45, and the port's own combat table src/characters/enemyBasics.js ('23', lines 1024-1025) correctly carries minDamage 20 / maxDamage 45. All ten other UNDEAD_DESIGNS level/damage pairs match EnemyBasics.cs exactly; only the Wraith min diverges.
consequence: The design metadata feeds only tools/paperdollViewer.js HUD labels (lines 860, 872), which display 'Wraith ... 10-45 damage' instead of 20-45; combat reads the separate enemyBasics.js table and is unaffected.

title: Silenced touch-caster re-arms melee timer: reset happens before the silence gate
claim: DFU DoTouchSpell resets the melee timer only after its whole condition passes, ending with SetReadySpell (EnemyMotor.cs:621-628), which returns false when silenced (EntityEffectManager.cs:315 SilenceCheck) - a silenced enemy's DoTouchSpell fails without touching MeleeTimer and its ordinary melee fires normally. The port's EnemyCaster.update resets attack.meleeTimer (enemyCasting.js:114) BEFORE returning the touch decision; the silence gate runs later in castEnemySpell (:159) and returns false with the timer already re-armed 1.5-3s. The arm re-fires every time the timer hits 0, usually beating the melee decision (which needs a classic tick plus the DFRandom roll on that exact frame).
consequence: Silence a touch-casting enemy (ghost, Frost Daedra, healer) and in the port it stands in melee range mostly not attacking - its melee timer perpetually re-armed by failed casts - where DFU's silenced caster falls back to normal melee attacks.

title: Bow shots always use RangedAttack1 records; HasRangedAttack2 mobiles should use records 25-29
claim: DFU picks the bow state: RangedAttack1 only if (HasRangedAttack1 && !HasRangedAttack2), else RangedAttack2 (EnemyMotor.cs:594-597); GetStateAnims maps RangedAttack2 to RangedAttack2Anims records 25-29 (DaggerfallMobileUnit.cs:840-841; EnemyBasics.cs:103-113). The port has a single 'ranged' state always returning RANGED_ATTACK1_ANIMS records 20-24 (mobileUnit.js:120), and hosts key one rangedStriking flag. Rows 130 (Battlemage) and 133 (Nightblade) carry hasRangedAttack2:true plus castsMagic (enemyBasics.js:2103, :2293), so hasBowAttack is true and their bow shots draw records 20-24 - which for these hasSpellAnimation rows are the SPELL-casting records.
consequence: A Battlemage or Nightblade shooting its bow renders its spell-casting sprite animation instead of its bow animation (archive 489/490 records 20-24 vs 25-29); the arrow still fires on the -1 marker.

title: Bow-band shots and spell casts not suppressed during knockback (CanAct chain incomplete)
claim: DFU KnockbackMovement sets CanAct=false while KnockbackSpeed>0 (EnemyMotor.cs:317) and TakeAction runs only under `if (CanAct)` (:171-172), so DoRangedAttack (:469 - the 1/32 bow and 1/40 spell rolls) and DoTouchSpell (:473) never run mid-knockback; the Hurt state also counts as IsPlayingOneShot (Base/MobileUnit.cs:153-168), blocking the rolls at :587. The port models only the giveUpTimer part of CanAct: the band arm (enemyAttack.js:127-134) and both EnemyCaster branches (enemyCasting.js:110-130) keep running while ai.knockbackSpeed>0; hosts gate only paralysis/hostility (dungeonContext.js:2290/2312, exteriorFoes.js:294/299). Melee correctly keeps running (CanAct-independent in DFU).
consequence: For the ~0.2-0.5s knockback window after each solid player hit, a port archer can loose its 1/32 bow shot and a caster can cast touch/ranged spells; DFU enemies cannot act at all during knockback - ranged foes fight back through hit-stun.

title: Detour override reordered ahead of DoRangedAttack in the decision chain
claim: DFU TakeAction calls DoRangedAttack at :469 and DoTouchSpell at :473 BEFORE the `if (avoidObstaclesTimer > 0) AttemptMove(...)` detour arm at :481-484, so an in-band shooter with sight+detection stands off and shoots even while a detour timer runs (the timer just decays). The port's _classicTick takes the detour arm first (enemyMotor.js:943-951) and only then calls _doRangedAttack (:956); its comment miscites :480-484 as "TakeAction's FIRST branch". test/audit24_wave35.test.js:113-114 pins this ordering ("the detour override first of all") - the pin restates the port, not the C#, which puts the detour after both attack calls.
consequence: For up to 0.75s after an obstacle/fall probe fires, an archer or ranged caster inside the 6-51.2 band with the target in sight keeps walking its detour instead of standing off as DFU does; shots still roll from the attack component, so it shoots on the move.

title: searchMult not reset when GiveUpTimer expires (or while pacified)
claim: DFU HandleNoAction resets searchMult=0 on ANY of its three arms - target null, GiveUpTimer <= 0, or PredictedTargetPos sentinel (EnemyMotor.cs:357-366, searchMult=0 at :362) - every FixedUpdate. The port resets it only on the predictedTargetPos===null arm (enemyMotor.js:935); the gave-up arm at :931 (`!detected && giveUpTimer <= 0`) returns without touching searchMult, and a pacified foe skips _classicTick entirely (:1039) so no arm runs. The stale ramp is only cleared later by _getDestination's clear-path arm (:869).
consequence: A foe that ramped its search (searchMult up to 10) then gave up resumes a later non-clear-path pursuit aiming up to 10 units past the last-known position instead of at it, walking somewhere DFU's freshly-reset foe would not.

title: Touch casts gated on the attack machine being Idle; DFU DoTouchSpell has no one-shot gate
claim: DFU's DoTouchSpell condition (EnemyMotor.cs:621-623) has no isPlayingOneShot term; the only one-shot early-out above it in TakeAction is OneShotPauseActionsWhilePlaying (:465), true only for SeducerTransform states (Base/MobileUnit.cs:174-184). So a DFU foe whose melee timer is 0 mid-swing casts the touch spell, ChangeEnemyState(Spell) cutting the swing. The port adds `idle` (attack.machine.state === 'Idle') to the touch arm (enemyCasting.js:107, :110), skipping the cast until the swing ends. Reachable when ResetMeleeTimer floors to 0: 1500 - 50*(level-10) + 450*(reflexes-2) <= 0, i.e. player level ~22+ at low reflexes, ~40 at average.
consequence: Against high-level players, a touch-caster in melee range delays its cast by up to a full swing (~0.5-1s) and its interrupted melee blow lands where DFU would have cancelled it into the spell.

title: GiveUpTimer frozen during paralysis/knockback; DFU UpdateTimers runs before the CanAct gate
claim: DFU UpdateTimers runs unconditionally every FixedUpdate, before `if (CanAct) TakeAction` (EnemyMotor.cs:170-172): detection refills GiveUpTimer to 200 (:419-420) and it decrements per classic tick while undetected (:423-424) even for a paralyzed or knocked-back foe (HandleParalysis/KnockbackMovement only clear CanAct). The port's refill/decrement lives inside _classicTick (enemyMotor.js:929-930), which is skipped while paralyzed or knocked (:1039 `if (!paralyzed && !knocked && this.isHostile)`), so the timer freezes for the whole paralysis.
consequence: A paralyzed foe whose player hides does not run down its 12.5s give-up window during the paralysis; when it wakes it resumes blind pursuit where DFU's foe would already have given up and stopped.

title: FACTION_TYPE_INDIVIDUAL is 3 but FactionTypes.Individual is 4 (3 is Subgroup)
claim: staticNpc.js:220 exports FACTION_TYPE_INDIVIDUAL = 3 and staticNpcName:209 tests fd.type === 3. DFU FactionFile.cs:537-538: Subgroup = 3, Individual = 4; StaticNPC.GetDisplayName (:319) tests type == Individual (4). The port's production faction dict agrees with DFU (src/formats/factionFile.js:17 Individual: 4; npcSession.js:62 same), so staticNpcName's check never matches a real Individual and instead matches Subgroup factions. Test pins (staticnpc.test.js:112 uses the constant; audit24_onehome.test.js:196 hardcodes type 3) restate the port, not the C#.
consequence: A named individual (King Gothryd, type 4) clicked in a palace shows a random generated name instead of the faction's fixed name; an NPC whose faction is a Subgroup (type 3, e.g. a knightly order) is named with the faction's own name string.

title: Static NPC generated names use the race's name bank; DFU always uses the region's
claim: staticNpcName defaults bank = bankForRace(data.race) (staticNpc.js:211). DFU: SetRuntimeData sets npcData.nameBank = GetNameBankOfCurrentRegion() (StaticNPC.cs:309, always Breton/Redguard) and GetDisplayName calls FullName(npcData.nameBank, gender) (:325-326); TalkManager.cs:2848 uses the region bank too; nothing assigns a race bank. Both production callers omit nameBank (worldModes.js:976, 1364). The port knows the law for mobiles (world.js:506, exterior.js:1367 pass getNameBankOfRegion citing MobilePersonNPC.cs:214) and staticNpc.js:233 re-exports getNameBankOfRegion, but no static caller uses it. Factions without a race: line parse race 0 = Nord on both sides.
consequence: Any interior static NPC whose derived race differs from the region race (incl. the Nord default on race-less factions) is named from the wrong bank - Nord '...sen' surnames in Breton/Redguard towns where DFU generates regional names.

title: Guild-popup Talk seam builds staticNpcData without race lookups: race is always Nord there
claim: talkToStaticNpcHere (worldModes.js:1361-1374, the GuildServicePopup Talk button / Spymaster dismissal) calls staticNpcData(pn, {...questSceneCtx(), buildingKey}); questSceneCtx returns only {mapId, locationIndex} (world.js:2808, exterior.js:1222-1225), so getFaction stays null and raceOfCurrentRegion defaults () => 0. raceFromFaction(fid!=0, null,...) then always yields Nord (staticNpc.js:139-141), and staticNpcName uses the Nord bank. The direct-click seam passes real lookups (questBridge.js:256-257; worldModes.js:890). DFU's GetRaceFromFaction (StaticNPC.cs:357-369) always has the live FactionData lookup and region fallback; the popup Talk reads the same StaticNPC.Data.
consequence: The same NPC answers a different generated name through the popup's Talk button than through a direct click (same seed, different bank/draw pattern), and every NPC on that path is stamped race Nord.

title: talkToStaticNPC gets the raw block record as data, so nameSeed reads 0 for every static NPC
claim: worldModes.js:979 and :1366 pass { data: pn, ... } where pn is the block-person record (no nameSeed field; nothing in src/ writes pn.nameSeed - the derived npcData with the real seed is computed at :890/:1363 and used only for displayName). npcSession.talkToStaticNPC reads targetNPC?.data?.nameSeed ?? 0 (npcSession.js:467) = 0 always; worldModes.js:1021/:1370 likewise pass npcSeed: pn.nameSeed ?? 0 into openTalkWindow. DFU passes the StaticNPC whose .Data carries the derived nameSeed (TalkManager.cs:759, :770). The audit24_onehome.test.js:225 pin asserts the '{ data: pn, ... }' shape - it restates the port.
consequence: castleNPCsSpokenTo is keyed by 0 (npcSession.js:564-573): the first castle NPC clicked consumes the only 25% work roll and no castle NPC can ever offer work after; talk-answer randomization is identical for every static NPC instead of per-person.

title: collectExteriorNpcs has no production caller: exterior static NPCs never exist
claim: collectExteriorNpcs ports RMBLayout's non-zero-FactionID rule (RMBLayout.cs:366-378, 442-454: SetRMBPeopleData + AddComponent<StaticNPC> + SetupIndividualStaticNPC on every exterior flat with FactionID != 0), but its only importer is test/names.test.js; neither exterior host reads flat factionIDs at all (grep of exterior.js/world.js: zero hits). Known open gap: Port-Ledger.md:338 records it and test/audit18_bible_docs.test.js:334-342 pins the no-caller state (the pin restates the port).
consequence: No exterior static NPC (factioned town flats) is ever an activation/talk/quest target outside; clicking one falls through as scenery, and quests binding individuals at exterior flats cannot land.

title: IsChildNPCData is unported; isChildNPC is read in three places and written nowhere
claim: DFU StaticNPC.IsChildNPCData (:342-350) flags children by IsChildNPCTexture(archive, record) or factionID == 514, gating quest offers (TalkManager.cs:755-770) and the work pool (:2842). The port has no equivalent: grep of src/ shows isChildNPC/isChild only read (worldModes.js:979,1366 pass !!pn.isChildNPC; npcSession.js:466,653) and never written, and staticNpc.js carries neither the 514 constant nor the child texture table. The flag is constant false.
consequence: A child NPC in a castle can pass the isCastleNpcOfferingQuest door and offer quests where DFU excludes children from both questor arms; the work-pool child exclusion is inert.

title: Billboard anim frame not reset to 0 on idle/move state switch
claim: DFU MobilePersonBillboard.SetIdle (:291-313) resets currentFrame = 0 and animTimer = 1 on every idle<->move transition, so each state starts at frame 0. The port's MobilePerson.update (mobilePerson.js:245-256) keeps one monotonically increasing this.frame and this._timer across state changes and takes frame % n, so a transition starts at an arbitrary phase of the new record's cycle.
consequence: A townsperson stopping to face the player (or resuming walking) starts the idle/walk cycle at a random frame instead of frame 0 - a small visible animation-phase divergence.

title: place() marks the spawn tile Occupied; DFU never flags a spawn tile
claim: MobilePerson.place (mobilePerson.js:127-141) calls nav.setOccupied(gx, gy) on the spawn cell. In DFU nothing flags the spawn tile: SpawnAvailableMobile only positions the transform (PopulationManager.cs:150-166), GetRandomSpawnPosition only tests weight > 0 (CityNavigation.cs:512-535), InitMotor resets nav positions without setting flags (:274-283), and Occupied is only ever set on TARGET tiles in SetTargetPosition (:438-439). GetNextNavPositionWeight treats Occupied as weight 0 (:528-529), which the port mirrors, so the extra flag changes the neighbour weights other walkers see.
consequence: Until a just-spawned (or spawn-idled) person picks its first target, other townsfolk read its tile as weight 0 and path around it where DFU walkers would enter it - a subtle crowd-flow divergence.

title: Unsheathe always plays clip 78; DFU plays the weapon's own equip sound
claim: weaponRig.toggleSheath() plays SOUND.DrawWeapon (78) for every real weapon (weaponRig.js:104; playerWeapon.js:77-82; soundClips.js:11 calls 78 the 'FPSWeapon.DrawWeaponSound default'). In DFU that default is dead: WeaponManager.SetWeapon (:780) overwrites DrawWeaponSound with weapon.GetEquipSound() whenever ApplyWeapon (:742-755) applies a weapon, and ToggleSheath -> PlayActivateSound plays that field (FPSWeapon.cs:295). GetEquipSound (DaggerfallUnityItem.cs:839-867) is per-type: 377/378/379/380/413/414/415/416 - none exist in the port's SOUND enum. The pin at test/weaponrig.test.js:31-37 restates the port, not the C#.
consequence: Every unsheathe of any real weapon plays the wrong clip: a flat draw sound 78 instead of DFU's weapon-specific equip clank (longsword 378, bow 416, etc.).

title: Bow viewmodel hidden during post-shot cooldown; DFU keeps it visible
claim: weaponRig.shown() returns false while `m.isBow && m.now < m.cooldownUntil` (weaponRig.js:75, 'bow cooldown hide'), so draw() skips the bow for the whole cooldown. DFU's WeaponManager.Update does `if (Time.time < cooldownTime) return;` (:230-233) BEFORE any ShowWeapons call - the early return leaves ScreenWeapon.ShowWeapon at its prior value (true, set at :290), so the bow stays drawn through the cooldown. Nothing in DFU hides a weapon for bow cooldown.
consequence: After every bow shot the port's bow art blinks out for the cooldown ((10*(100-speed)+800)/980 s, ~1.3s at speed 50) and pops back; DFU shows a steady idle bow.

title: Weapon stays drawn during the equip-delay pause; DFU hides it
claim: During an equip countdown DFU calls ShowWeapons(false) and returns (WeaponManager.cs:276-281), hiding the screen weapon until the delay expires. The rig ports only the attack-block half: attackInput/clickAttack test entity.equipCountdown (weaponRig.js:96,100, CH3 comment citing :276-278) and frame() drains it at dt*980 (:116-118, matching :679), but shown() (weaponRig.js:71-77) never consults equipCountdown, so draw() keeps rendering the newly equipped weapon through the pause. equip.js:56 sets entity.equipCountdown on every equip, so the state is reachable.
consequence: After swapping to a heavy weapon (EquipDelayTimes up to 5000) the port shows the new weapon immediately while silently refusing attacks; DFU shows empty hands for the delay - the player's cue the swap is in progress.

title: Jump gate misses the WasClimbing bypass; climbing.js wasClimbing is computed and never read
claim: AcrobatMotor.HandleJumpInput:76 gates the jump with `if (!climbingMotor.WasClimbing && playerMotor.GroundedTime < 0.1f) return;` - a player who was climbing at the start of this frame's check may jump with zero grounded time. The port's gate (motor.js:649) is `this.grounded && input.jump && this.groundedTime >= GROUNDED_JUMP_GATE_S && !this.slowFalling` with no climbing bypass. The port DOES track the flag - climbing.js:119 writes `this.wasClimbing = this.isClimbing` every step - but grep of src/ shows no reader anywhere: a ported member with no caller.
consequence: Topping out or aborting a climb onto ground then pressing Jump: DFU jumps instantly, the port refuses the jump for the next 0.1 s of grounded time.

title: Over-encumbered swimmer forced sink missing from the swim path
claim: LevitateMotor.Update:83-85: `overEncumbered = (CarriedWeight * 4 > 250) && !playerLevitating && !GodMode; if (playerSwimming && overEncumbered && !climbingMotor.IsClimbing && !IsWaterWalking) upDownVector += Vector3.down; else if (Jump/FloatUp)...` - the sink REPLACES the float keys, so an over-encumbered swimmer is pushed down every frame and cannot float up. The port's swim path (motor.js:530-531) reads only `input.up`/`input.down` from the host's keys; no host or motor code computes carried weight for the swim path (grep for encumb/CarriedWeight in src/scenes and src/player finds none feeding the motor).
consequence: Carrying more than 62.5 kg while swimming: DFU drags the player to the bottom and blocks surfacing; the port swims and surfaces freely regardless of load.

title: Crouch stays live while levitating; no forced stand for a crouched levitator
claim: DFU DecideHeightAction: while levitating a crouched player is forced to DoStanding (PlayerHeightChanger.cs:137-145), and the crouch-press block is nested under `else if (!riding && !onWater && !levitating)` (:171), so the Crouch press does nothing while levitating. The port's _heightAction first arm (motor.js:358) is `input.crouch && (!this.swimming || this.grounded)` with no levitating term and no forced-stand arm, so the crouch toggle fires while levitating and a crouched player who starts levitating stays crouched.
consequence: In the port a levitating player can toggle the 0.9 crouch capsule mid-air (fitting through gaps DFU forbids) and a crouched levitator keeps crouch speed/eye; DFU forces standing and ignores the key.

title: Climbing does not force a crouched player to stand
claim: DFU DecideHeightAction's second arm in the on-foot block: `else if (climbing) { timerMax = timerMedium; if (crouching) heightAction = DoStanding; forcedSwimCrouch = false; }` (PlayerHeightChanger.cs:184-191) - climbing forces the standing capsule every frame. The port's _heightAction (motor.js:352-368) has only the crouch-press, swim-force, and swim-unforce arms; nothing reads the climb state, and ClimbingState.step/_climbStep have no crouch gate, so a crouched player climbs crouched and remains crouched after topping out.
consequence: A crouched climber in the port keeps the 0.9 capsule and crouched eye through and after the climb (and can climb under 0.9-1.8 clearances); DFU stands the player up on the medium (0.25 s) clock as the climb starts.

title: Outdoor hosts pass no pitch and no up/down: levitation above ground cannot change height
claim: LevitateMotor.Update:71-91 moves along the camera look (pitch included) and reads Jump/FloatUp for up, Crouch/FloatDown for down - everywhere. The motor implements this (motor.js:520-531; contract at :299-301) and the dungeon hosts wire it (dungeon.js:400-403 and worldModes.js:2660-2663 pass up/down and cam.pitch). But both outdoor hosts call player.update with only {forward, strafe, run, sneak, jump, crouch} and cam.yaw - no up/down, no pitch (exterior.js:1482-1489; world.js:3135-3142) - while shared.js:382 sets player.levitating outdoors each frame. With pitch defaulting 0 and up/down undefined, my is always 0 in the levitate branch and velY is forced 0.
consequence: Cast Levitate outdoors (spell 14,255 exists in the port): the player hovers frozen at current height - no key and no look direction can ascend or descend until the effect expires. In DFU levitation works identically indoors and out.

title: Crouch key does not drive float-down while swimming/levitating in any host
claim: LevitateMotor.Update:86-89: `else if (HasAction(Jump) || HasAction(FloatUp)) up; else if (HasAction(Crouch) || HasAction(FloatDown)) down;` - the held Crouch key dives a swimmer and descends a levitator. The motor's own contract states this (motor.js:300: 'up/down: the Jump/FloatUp and Crouch/FloatDown keys, HELD'), but every host maps only FloatDown: dungeon.js:401 and worldModes.js:2661 both pass `down: held(keys, 'FloatDown')`, and the outdoor hosts pass nothing. The hosts' up arm does match (jumpHeld || FloatUp).
consequence: Holding Crouch (C) while swimming does nothing in the port (only PageDown dives); in DFU it dives. Combined with the missing levitate gate in _heightAction, Crouch while levitating toggles the stance instead of descending.

title: Slowfall constant velocity is fixed-rate-coupled: 1.75 m/s vs DFU's 2.1 m/s
claim: AcrobatMotor.ApplyGravity:187 sets `moveDirection.y = -slowFallSpeed * Time.deltaTime` in FixedUpdate, i.e. a fall VELOCITY of 105 * fixedDeltaTime; DFU's ProjectSettings/TimeManager.asset:6 pins Fixed Timestep 0.02, so DFU slowfalls at 2.1 m/s. The port copies the shape verbatim (motor.js:670 `velY = -SLOWFALL_SPEED * dt`) but steps at FIXED_DT = 1/60 (motor.js:73), giving 1.75 m/s. The 60 Hz step is a documented port choice, but slowfall is the one law whose observable magnitude changes with that rate, and the pin motorStairs.test.js:295 asserts -105/60, restating the port without noting DFU's 0.02.
consequence: Slow Falling descents are ~17% slower than DFU (2.1 -> 1.75 m/s); timing-sensitive drops under the buff take 20% longer. Fall damage is unaffected (slowfall re-anchors fallStart each tick in both).

title: Missile impact flash (record 1, one-shot, 15fps) is ported as a constant but never spawned
claim: DFU DoCollision (DaggerfallMissile.cs:365-369) swaps the missile billboard to the impact anim - UseSpellBillboardAnims(1, true) = record 1, OneShot, fps 15 (:45) - and the missile persists 0.6s (:47) so it plays. The port defines IMPACT_FPS = 15 (flatAnimation.js:33) and states the law in its header (:29-33), but nothing in src/ consumes it: both missile hosts destroy the billboard at impact with no record-1 spawn (hostMagic.js:363-371 retireMissile, called :404/:421/:432; dungeonContext.js:1592-1604, called :1618/:1630). explodeAt (hostMagic.js:208-217) is damage-only. Pin test/flatanim.test.js:182-199 asserts constants only.
consequence: Every spell missile (player and enemy, all scenes) vanishes on impact with no contact flash; DFU plays the 0.6s record-1 animation at 15fps on every hit.

title: renderCharacterSprite leaks gl.clearColor(0,0,0,0) into every subsequent frame
claim: renderCharacterSprite (renderer.js:746-761) sets gl.clearColor(0,0,0,0) at :751 for the sprite FBO and restores framebuffer, viewport and proj/view - but not the clear color. The only other clearColor call is the constructor's one-time (0.53,0.7,0.92,1.0) at :618; beginFrame (:1095-1104) clears without setting it. After the first frame that renders a rig sprite (exterior.js:1685; dungeon foes via dungeonContext.js:1396), every later beginFrame clears the canvas transparent; with default alpha:true (:445 passes only {antialias:false}) uncovered pixels show the page background (#000, index.html:8).
consequence: Uncovered pixels render page-black instead of the intended clear color after the first character-sprite frame - visible only before the sky panorama loads and in skyless scenes; negligible but a genuine unrestored-GL-state leak.

title: Guard killed by fall damage brands the player a murderer
claim: The fall arm (cityGuards.js:356-363) routes through damageGuard, whose death branch unconditionally sets playerEntity.crimeCommitted = CRIME_MURDER (:274). DFU's EnemyMotor.ApplyFallDamage (EnemyMotor.cs:1398-1401) calls DecreaseHealth directly; Murder is assigned only in DaggerfallEntityBehaviour.HandleAttackFromSource (:263-269) inside the sourceEntityBehaviour == PlayerEntityBehaviour gate (:203), so a fall death never sets a crime. The pin test/audit24_wave36.test.js:142 asserts the port's line with 'so death and crime fire' while citing only ApplyFallDamage, which carries no crime - the pin restates the port.
consequence: A watchman who dies falling while chasing the player escalates the active crime to Murder without the player striking, inflating the court's penalty rolls for a kill the player never made.

title: Witness/countdown half of spawnCityGuards has no production caller
claim: The non-immediate arm (cityGuards.js:196-238; countdown consumed :325-328) is called with immediate=false only by test/cityguards.test.js:81. Both hosts pass true only (world.js:1030, exterior.js:625) and the quest SpawnCityGuards action is a pended guard pattern (systems/quest/actions.js:2672). DFU's false-mode callers are PlayerEntity.cs:500-503 (LegalRep < -10, 5% per game-hour, Criminal_Conspiracy) and :507-510 (banished flag, 10%); grep of src/ finds no port counterpart of either arm.
consequence: The witness law - civilians seeing a crime, guard NPCs converting on sight, guards arriving after a 5-10s countdown - and passive guard responses to low-legal-rep/banished characters never run in the shipped game.

title: Encounter-foe melee hits skip the player pain voice in ?world
claim: world.js gives cityGuards.onPlayerHurt playPlayerVoice(playerPainVoice(...)) (:903) and the enemy-arrow arm likewise (:3461), but exteriorFoes' onPlayerHurt (world.js:919-924) does only hurtPlayer + hit sound + surfacePlayer - no pain voice. In DFU every enemy melee hit goes through EnemyAttack.SendDamageToPlayer (EnemyAttack.cs:404-406) whose SendMessage("RemoveHealth") reaches PlayerFootsteps.RemoveHealth (PlayerFootsteps.cs:348-364), the 40% pain cry, regardless of attacker type. dungeonContext plays it on both melee arms (:1702, :1946); the gap is exactly the main host's encounter pool.
consequence: In the shipped game path (menu boots bootWorld), a bandit's or monster's blow never makes the player cry out while a guard blow and an enemy arrow do - an audible inconsistency DFU does not have.

title: Acquittal applies no vitals restore - player leaves court at 1 HP
claim: The verdict 'free' arm (arrestFlow.js:142-149) calls clearArrest() only; the comment at :235-237 asserts acquittal takes clearArrest alone because the floor 'belongs to release'. DFU's acquittal arm calls FillVitalSigns explicitly (DaggerfallCourtWindow.cs:423-425). Surrender forces health to 1 first (PlayerEntity.cs:2321; the port's setHealth1 hook at arrestFlow.js:69/77), so the acquitted player holds exactly 1 HP. The 'full refill pends vitals wiring' note covers only release() (:240); the acquittal arm is excluded from even that by its own comment, so the debt stays unpaid when vitals wiring lands.
consequence: A player who surrenders and wins the case steps outside at 1 HP where DFU restores full vitals - and unlike the other court arms this gap is asserted correct, not tracked as pending.

title: paintOverlay.js is dead code; the ?paint flag dead-ends
claim: mountPaintOverlay is the module's only export and nothing in src/ or test/ imports it (grep: zero importers). The ?paint URL flag is read at world.js:2864, destructured in worldModes.js:266, forwarded into buildInteriorContext's opts at worldModes.js:2233 - but interiorContext.js reads only opts.peopleVisible/opts.setupStaticNpc/opts.voxelfolk (:198/:225/:239); opts.paint is never consumed.
consequence: The C6L body-sheet paint tuner (154 lines) is unreachable: ?paint is accepted, threaded through two hosts, and silently does nothing.

title: Guard fall damage plays no blood splash
claim: The guard fall arm (cityGuards.js:356-364) plays SOUND.FallDamage and bills damage but never calls hitEffects.showBloodSplash, although hitEffects is a module dep (:88). DFU shows ShowBloodSplash(0, transform.position) on every enemy fall past the threshold (EnemyMotor.cs:1403-1407), and the port's sibling pool has the call (exteriorFoes.js:275).
consequence: A falling watchman bleeds in DFU and in the port's encounter pool but not in the guard pool - a visible asymmetry on the same law.

title: Sourceless damage (fall) flips a pacified encounter foe hostile
claim: damageFoe's first line (exteriorFoes.js:181-182) makes any non-hostile foe hostile and seeds pursuit of the player on ANY damage; the fall arm (:264-277) routes through it with no player involvement. In DFU, ApplyFallDamage calls DecreaseHealth only (EnemyMotor.cs:1400-1401); hostility flips live in HandleAttackFromSource under the player-source gate (DaggerfallEntityBehaviour.cs:203, 250-261), so a fall never re-hostiles a pacified enemy.
consequence: A language-pacified foe that takes fall damage (>5m drop) turns hostile and hunts the player with no player action; narrow but reachable on exterior terrain.

title: computeTier discards questionType: every question gets the +5 LocalBuilding reaction mod
claim: computeTier (townTalk.js:434-447) takes (questionType, socialGroup) but line 435 is `void questionType;` and line 440 hardcodes `questionIndex: 0`. C# TalkManager.cs:1994-1995 passes listItem.questionType into GetReactionToPlayer_0_1_2, whose :664-667 adds questionTypeReactionMods[GetClassicQuestionIndex(qt)] = {5,0,0,0,5,0,0,0} (:96): +5 only for LocalBuilding/Regional and QuestLocation/OrganizationInfo, 0 for Person/Thing/Work/QuestPerson/QuestItem. The port's mapper exists (answerPipeline.js:115) and the table is pinned (talkTopics.js:290), and the pipeline passes questionType to this seam (answerPipeline.js:259, world.js:2585) - computeTier throws it away.
consequence: When the first answer after a tone change is a Person/Work/Tell-me-about question, reaction is 5 higher than DFU and the inflated value is cached in toneReactionForTalkSession for the session - e.g. Work banding to 8076/8077 where DFU refuses with 8075.

title: Static-NPC conversations roll the reaction tier with the last MOBILE NPC's seed (or 0)
claim: computeTier's rollToBeat seed is `npcSeed: _talkNpc?._talkSeed ?? 0` (townTalk.js:439); `_talkNpc` is assigned only in the mobile activate() path (:301). The static path (worldModes.js:1021/:1370 -> openTalkWindow) forwards its per-NPC nameSeed to the answer/knowledge hooks but never to computeTier. C# TalkManager.cs:669-673 seeds DFRandom by lastTargetStaticNPC.GetHashCode() for static NPCs, stable per partner - and the port's own stand-in law (townTalk.js:297-299, Ledger A) is a stable per-person seed. Here every static NPC shares seed 0 on a fresh boot, then inherits whichever townsperson was talked to last.
consequence: All guild/temple/questor conversations share one reaction-band roll until a mobile talk happens, and the same static NPC's band shifts after an unrelated street conversation - DFU's band is stable per NPC.

title: fatigueLossMultiplierFor omits the ImprovedAthleticism 0.8 arm inside the C# region it cites
claim: shared.js:843-846 cites PlayerEntity.cs:388-400 and returns 0.9 for career Athleticism else 1.0. The C# at :397-400 is `fatigueLossMultiplier = ImprovedAthleticism ? 0.8f : 0.9f`. The port decodes the ImprovesTalents enchantment into entity._enchantMods.improvedAthleticism (enchantments.js:433-440, applied at :655) but no reader consumes it - a law computed and thrown away. The only pend flag in the area (skills.js:94) names the JUMP +0.1 term, not the fatigue multiplier.
consequence: An Athleticism character wearing an Improved Athleticism item loses fatigue at 0.9x instead of DFU's 0.8x - the enchantment's fatigue benefit does nothing.

title: A failed night-panorama build permanently wedges the sky controller's pending guard
claim: createSkyController.use(): `pending = key; ... buildPanorama(...).then(apply)` (shared.js:178,194) has no .catch, and the NIGHT branch of buildPanorama (:137-149) awaits fetchBytes for the NITE IMG and its palette with no try/catch - unlike its day-sky sibling (:152-162), which catches and degrades to the gradient. On a rejected fetch, apply never runs, pending stays equal to that key, and every later use() for the same key returns at :177 (`key === pending`) - never retried, plus an unhandled rejection. Recovery only when a DIFFERENT key is requested (dawn). DFU reads local files and has no one-shot guard to wedge.
consequence: One failed NITE fetch at nightfall (lean data set, transient IndexedDB/network error) freezes the sky on the last day frame for the whole night with no retry.

title: Pickpocket 'found nothing valuable' uses the variant picker where DFU uses GetRandomText
claim: activate() passes `nothingText: () => randomVariant(FOUND_NOTHING_VALUABLE_TEXT_ID,...)` (townTalk.js:281-283) - a SubrecordSeparator-variant pick over plainText. C# PlayerActivate.cs:1645 uses TextProvider.GetRandomText(8999), pooling every Text TOKEN of the record (TextProvider.cs:250-269). The port built randomTextById for exactly this distinction and exposes it on this module (townTalk.js:679-681), but this site was not migrated. The two agree only if every 8999 variant is a single one-line token (unverifiable - no ARENA2 data here).
consequence: The no-gold pickpocket message draws from a differently-shaped pool than DFU's; a multi-line variant would print all its lines fused where DFU prints one.

title: %oth in the fallback question/answer chain uses the variant picker; DFU's Oath macro is GetRandomText
claim: expandRecord's oath (townTalk.js:168) and answerText's oath (:554) use `randomVariant(oathTextId(npcRace), '')`. C# resolves %oth via TalkManagerMCP.Oath() -> TextProvider.GetRandomText(201 + oathId) (TalkManagerMCP.cs:133-143), the flat token pool. The port's randomText accessor (:679-681) is documented as '%oth's seam' and the engine path consumes it (world.js:2303), but these two local sites stayed on randomVariant. textRsc.js:131-134 itself says the oath records hold 'several one-line oaths' in one record - the shape where the two pickers diverge. Scope: the pre-engine fallback paths, live in the ?exterior host (its createTownTalk passes no talkEngine, exterior.js:470-486).
consequence: In ?exterior, a greeting/question or where-is answer carrying %oth can render the whole oath list (or a mis-weighted pick) instead of one random oath line.

title: Steal mode says 'You are too far away' to an already-pickpocketed NPC; DFU is silent
claim: tryActivate gates steal distance before the attempted check (townTalk.js:269), with pickpocketAttempted tested only later inside activate() (:278). C# ActivateMobileNPC's Steal arm nests the distance test INSIDE `if (!mobileNpc.PickpocketByPlayerAttempted)` (PlayerActivate.cs:786-799), so an already-attempted NPC produces no output at any distance.
consequence: Activating an already-pickpocketed townsperson from beyond 3.2m in Steal mode prints a 'too far away' message DFU never shows.

title: Dungeon drowning deals zero damage: 3-arg call into the local 1-arg hurtPlayer wrapper
claim: breathTick's drowned arm calls hurtPlayer(playerEntity, playerEntity.health, { bypassShield: true }) (:2045), but the LOCAL hurtPlayer (:1030-1032) takes ONE arg (dmg) and forwards hurtEntity(playerEntity, dmg). So dmg = the playerEntity OBJECT; playerEntity.js:97's guard `if (!(dmg > 0)) return false` sees object>0 -> NaN -> false, and returns having done nothing. The call shape was copied from world.js:637 where hurtPlayer IS the 3-arg import (world.js:110); here the import is aliased hurtEntity (:26) and shadowed by the wrapper. The :2043 comment claims this exact bug class was already review-fixed.
consequence: PlayerEntity.cs:339-340 does SetHealth(0) at 0 breath; in the port a player out of breath underwater in a dungeon takes no damage at all - drowning can never hurt or kill. Only breathStep's unit test pins the systems half; no test pins this host call.

title: Runtime-spawned dungeon foes (rest encounters, quest CreateFoe) never get spell lists or a caster
claim: assignEnemySpells + EnemyCaster minting runs ONCE over the load-time foes array (:691-696). _spawnEncounter (:913-928) and spawnQuestFoe (:630-636) call buildFoeAt (:479), which never assigns spells; the frame loop's cast arm reads f.caster (:2312) - undefined for those foes. DFU's SetEnemyCareer assigns the spell lists on EVERY spawn (EnemyEntity.cs:350-386) and SetEnemySpells also pins magicka = 10*level+100 and four magic skills to 80 (:453-461); the port's makeEnemyEntity does neither. The port's own exterior pool assigns per-spawn inside its build path (exteriorFoes.js:107-109), so this host is the odd one out.
consequence: An Imp, Orc Shaman, Vampire, Lich, or CastsMagic class enemy spawned by a dungeon rest interruption or placed by a quest never casts a single spell and has no caster magicka pool; the same enemy at a load-time marker, or spawned outdoors, casts normally.

title: Standalone dungeon fly-cam is dead code: `else if (!held)` tests the imported input helper
claim: dungeon.js:427 gates the fly-cam WASD block with `} else if (!held) {`, but `held` there is the FUNCTION imported from ui/input.js (:33, used as held(keys,'Jump') at :367) - always truthy, so !held is always false and the branch never runs. Sibling hosts use a bare `} else {` (exterior.js:1545, world.js:3215). worldModes.js:2744's comment shows the drift: an old dungeon.js line used a local boolean `held` later renamed overlayHeld (:353), leaving this stale reference resolving to the import. Port-internal bug, no C# counterpart; no test pins it.
consequence: With ?dungeon&fly (the file's own documented mode, :103-105) or ?shot without probe pokes, WASD/Shift never moves the camera - the fly-cam is frozen at spawn; look still works. Shot-mode probes (__move/__pose) still function.

title: Player arrow hits play no hit sound and show no blood splash
claim: The fromPlayer arrow-impact arm (:1641-1674) on dmg>0 plays only enemyPainVoice and calls damageFoe with the knock direction. DFU routes a player arrow through WeaponManager.WeaponDamage with arrowHit=true (DaggerfallMissile.cs:681-687), whose damage>0 arm plays the enemy-side hit sound (:562-567) and ShowBloodSplash at the impact (:569-573) before knockback and the 40% voice - the same arm the port's own MELEE path mirrors at :1538 (hitSoundFor) and :1544 (showBloodSplash). The port fixed the mirror direction (enemy arrow -> player: sound+flash+cry, wave 46 at :1699-1703) but left the player->foe direction without its two counterparts. No test pins arrow sound/blood.
consequence: Every landed player arrow in a dungeon is silent and bloodless while every melee hit thuds and splashes - an audible/visible divergence from DFU on the primary ranged weapon.

title: Enemy arrow that reaches the player with a failed damage roll is silent
claim: The enemy-arrow-at-player arm (:1676-1707) plays hit sound/flash/cry only under `if (dmg > 0)` (:1699-1703) and nothing otherwise. DFU's BowDamage (:141) goes through ApplyDamageToPlayer, whose else arm plays sounds.PlayMissSound(weapon) on damage <= 0 (EnemyAttack.cs:297-298). The port's own MELEE arm has this else (:1937 enemyMissSound); the arrow arm does not.
consequence: A dodged enemy arrow (contact but failed to-hit roll) makes no sound; DFU rings the miss whoosh from the shooter. Small audible divergence.

title: destroy() never frees the magic engine's in-flight spell-missile batches
claim: dungeonContext.destroy() (:3048-3070) frees billboardBatches, foe batches, corpses, the host missiles list (:3064) and dropped piles, but the player-magic engine minted at :1117 keeps its own missiles/batches lists (hostMagic.js:78-93), freed only on per-missile retire (:360-368), and exposes no destroy surface; nothing in destroy() reaches them. Port-internal teardown gap under the 17e-F29 'every allocation has an owner' rule this same function cites.
consequence: Exiting a dungeon (worldModes calls dungeonCtx.destroy() at :2557/:3944) while a player spell missile is still flying leaks that missile's VAO+buffers, repeatable per enter/cast/exit cycle. Narrow window (8s missile lifespan); no visible symptom short of long-session GPU growth.

title: Duplicate hudCtx.toggleRest key makes the S40 outdoor-rest wiring dead code in both hosts
claim: hudCtx defines toggleRest twice (world.js:1922 '() => toggleRest()' and :1932 '() => toggleExteriorRest()'; identically exterior.js:1016/:1027). The later key wins, so every Rest route (ladder :1969/:1983, large-HUD panel) reaches toggleExteriorRest, and the S40 path - toggleRest (world.js:1423, exterior.js:669) with its outdoorRestDeps bag (world.js:1377-1422, exterior.js:636-668) carrying tickQuests, the resting-variant areEnemiesNearby, endLines, onClose - never runs. Neither bag is a superset (only the live bag has the encounter catch-up, world.js:983). Conflicting pins: restlodging.test.js:576/:589/:845-847 pin the dead wiring; restwhere.test.js:170/:173 pin the live one.
consequence: A generation of rest fixes (quest ticking, the resting enemy law, rest-end text) is silently disabled in both above-ground hosts; two test files pin contradictory wirings and both pass.

title: Outdoor rest never ticks the quest machine - DFU ticks it every 10-minute sub-tick
claim: DFU TickRest (DaggerfallRestWindow.cs:376-379) calls QuestMachine.Instance.Tick() inside every RaiseTime sub-tick. The port's RestSession does the same through deps.tickQuests (restSession.js:389-404), but the live path opens RestWindow with exteriorRestDeps (world.js:1861) whose bag (world.js:960-984) has no tickQuests - only the dead outdoorRestDeps (world.js:1384) carries it. The frame-level quest tick is gated on !townTalk.overlayActive (world.js:3097) and the rest window occupies that overlay (townTalk.js:700), so a rested night runs zero quest ticks.
consequence: Quest clocks, popups and CreateFoe ambush waves never fire during an outdoor rest - the wired abortRestForEnemySpawn seam (world.js:2845) cannot trigger from a quest wave, and all quest events land in one burst after waking.

title: Live rest path asks 'any guard alive?' instead of AreEnemiesNearby(resting) in both hosts
claim: DFU gates rest OPEN (DaggerfallUI.cs:652) and the hourly break (RestWindow.cs:403) on AreEnemiesNearby(true), which skips enemies that cannot see the player and are >12 units away, else requires canSee || WouldBeSpawnedInClassic (GameManager.cs:698-705). The port has this law (encounters.js:177-185) but the live deps bypass it: world.js:975-976 answers cityGuards.activeCount()>0 (all non-dead guards, no distance/sight test - cityGuards.js:113) OR foe detected/dist<=12; exterior.js:936 answers activeCount()>0 alone. Only the dead bags (world.js:1391, exterior.js:647) call the resting variant; the dead bag's own comment (world.js:1386-1390) names the live behavior 'a different rule'.
consequence: Once guards exist anywhere in town, every R press answers TEXT.RSC 354 and raises the enemy alert, and an in-progress rest breaks at the next hour - even when every guard is unaware and across the city; DFU allows the rest.

title: Rest deps pass 'textLines' where the factory reads 'endLines' - every rest ends silently
claim: createRestDeps composes the window's text lookup only from rest.endLines (shared.js:1177), and plainLines(undefined) is null (shared.js:667-669). The live bags supply the lookup under the wrong key - 'textLines: (id) => townTalk.lines(id)' at world.js:963 and exterior.js:931 - which nothing reads, so deps.endLines(id) is null for every id. RestWindow._end then takes the null-text branch and closes silently (restWindow.js:311-327), and the >99-hours notice (restWindow.js:267) is null too. DFU EndRest shows a box on every arm: 353/350/349/354 (RestWindow.cs:450-505). The dead outdoorRestDeps used the correct key (world.js:1409, exterior.js:657).
consequence: Outdoor rests end with no 'You wake up.'/'You are healed.' box, a rest broken by enemies closes without the 354 warning, and entering >99 hours silently resets the field instead of showing TEXT.RSC 26.

title: Exhaustion collapse asks only guard activeCount - encounter foes ignored, sight law bypassed
claim: DFU decides rest-vs-death on GameManager.AreEnemiesNearby() (PlayerEntity.cs:2397) - hostile enemies that see the player or would spawn in classic - and SetHealth(0) when true (PlayerEntity.cs:2440-2441). world.js:623 passes enemiesNearby: (cityGuards?.activeCount?.() ?? 0) > 0 into exhaustionOutcome - the exteriorFoes pool is not consulted at all (the same file's rest deps consult both pools, world.js:975-976), and activeCount has no sight/distance test. exterior.js:401 has the same coarse guard-only read. systems/rest.js:83-93 confirms enemiesNearby:true is the death arm.
consequence: Collapsing beside a detected encounter wolf yields the safe one-hour sleep instead of DFU's death; collapsing in town while one unaware guard is active anywhere kills the player where DFU grants the hour of rest.

title: ?exterior rest verdict hardcodes inTownOutside:true - non-town locations criminalize camping
claim: exterior.js:955-960 answers canRest({ inTownOutside: true, inTownLocation: false }) on the grounds the page 'IS a location'. But IsPlayerInTown(true,true) is a location-TYPE test over seven types (PlayerGPS.cs:507-513); for a Graveyard, DungeonRuin, Coven or HomePoor exterior - loadable via ?region/?loc, as the host's populatesWanderingNpcs gate (exterior.js:1353) acknowledges - CanRest falls to its free tail (RestWindow.cs:598). The host holds the correct test (_isPlayerInTownStrict, exterior.js:631) but only the dead deps use it. restwhere.test.js:179-182 pins the hardcoded literal with the same mistaken rationale (pin restates the port).
consequence: Resting at any non-town location on the ?exterior page charges Vagrancy, shows the illegal-camping warning and spawns guards, where DFU opens the rest window freely.

title: Crime clears on map-pixel exit, not on location-rect exit
claim: DFU clears CrimeCommitted in PlayerGPS_OnExitLocationRect (PlayerEntity.cs:2449-2452), raised on leaving the location's world rect widened by 4096 units (PlayerGPS.cs:677-679, 687-695 - whose comment says a player can be in a location's pixel yet outside the rect). The port's syncTopics clears via clearCrimeOnLocationExit on any change of the current PIXEL key (world.js:846-849; court.js:391-395 clears whenever the key changes), claiming 'this crossing IS DFU's OnExitLocationRect'. The same file's AUDIT-24 note (world.js:679-694) corrected exactly this rect-vs-pixel conflation for _musicInLocationRect's consumers, but the crime clear was not converted.
consequence: After a town crime, walking beyond the city rect but staying in the same 32768-unit pixel keeps crimeCommitted set - guards keep responding - until a pixel border, where DFU clears it at the widened town edge.

title: Encounter roll's inLocationRect is 'pixel has a location', not IsPlayerInLocationRect
claim: DFU's IntermittentEnemySpawn branches on PlayerGPS.IsPlayerInLocationRect (PlayerEntity.cs:567) - the widened world-coordinate rect - location-at-night arm inside it, wilderness day/night arms outside (PlayerEntity.cs:564-596). runEncounterTick passes inLocationRect: locationIndex.has(key) (world.js:995-998), i.e. 'the player's map pixel carries a location', which the file's own AUDIT-24 note (world.js:679-688) establishes is a different, up-to-7x-wider predicate. The true rect answer (_musicInLocationRect, world.js:689-694) exists and is unused here; encounters.js:107-118 consumes the flag exactly as the C# branches.
consequence: In the wilderness ring of any location-bearing pixel, daytime encounters never roll (the location arm rolls only at night) and night rolls use the location table/distance instead of the wilderness ones.

title: Native trade never removes sold/staged items from the player's pack - sell pays while the item stays
claim: packItems returns a filtered COPY (worldModes.js:698), so NativeTradeWindow._move (nativeTrade.js:150-154, staging at :195) splices a transient array and the item never leaves playerEntity.items; commitTrade's Sell/SellMagic arm (worldModes.js:744-754) pays and pushes staged items to the shelf WITHOUT removing them from the pack, and the Identify arms (:766-783) re-addItem items still held. DFU moves the item out of PlayerEntity.Items at the click (DaggerfallTradeWindow.cs:795/:824 TransferItem) and Sell's confirm clears remoteItems (:1051). The port's keyed doSell (:809-811) DOES splice the pack - the two sell paths disagree; test/nativetrade.test.js:24 shows the live-array contract.
consequence: Sell an item through the native trade screen: paid full price, item stays in the pack - repeatable unlimited gold. Identify pushes a second aliased reference into the pack (inventory.js:135-143). Staged items show in both lists at once.

title: forceExitToExterior skips cacheInteriorScene - recall/teleport out of a building discards interior state
claim: tryExit calls cacheInteriorScene() before teardown (worldModes.js:2434, matching PlayerEnterExit.cs:860); forceExitToExterior (:3937-3948) destroys the interior context with no cache write. DFU's Teleport caches the interior scene before departing (Teleport.cs:148-149, SaveLoadManager.CacheScene(playerEnterExit.Interior.name) when inside a building). Reachable via anchor recall (world.js:1143), the guild Teleportation service (world.js:1522), and quest TeleportPc respawn (world.js:1550).
consequence: Recalling/teleporting out of a building loses all interior changes since entry: next visit restores the stale pre-entry cache (bought goods reappear on the shelf as the same object references the player carries) or fresh block state; opened doors re-close.

title: worldModes runs the player motor under an open window; the standalone dungeon host freezes it
claim: frame() calls player.update every modal frame, with zeroed inputs when overlayHeld (worldModes.js:2654) - gravity, velocity and the crouch input (`crouch: crouchHeld && !latch.crouch` in the held arm) keep running under a window. dungeon.js gates the whole motor behind `if (walkMode && !overlayHeld)` (dungeon.js:353-357, 'no movers, no motor'). DFU pauses the game for any PauseWhileOpen window (UserInterfaceManager.cs:179-184 AddWindow -> PauseGame(true)), which worldModes' own comment (:2631-2634) cites as the law. Zeroed inputs are right for paralysis only.
consequence: Open a window mid-fall in a world-hosted interior/dungeon: the fall completes under the paused menu and fall damage lands (applyFallLanding :2708); a swimmer keeps sinking; the crouch key toggles crouch under a window. The standalone host and DFU both freeze.

title: Shelves in a broken-into CLOSED shop open the Buy trade window; DFU opens the stealing inventory
claim: DFU gates shelf activation on IsPlayerInsideOpenShop (PlayerActivate.cs:887-899): open -> Buy trade window; closed -> InventoryWindow.SetShopShelfStealing. The port computes insideOpenShop at the door (worldModes.js:2205-2207, PlayerActivate.cs:1120 verbatim) but feeds it only to the people gate and drops it; openShelf (:634-647) checks only isShop and always stocks + opens the Buy window. A closed shop is enterable via the steal-mode lockpick ladder (:2167-2188). The shoplifting FORMULA is a recorded pending (crime arc), but DFU never opens a paying trade window in a closed shop regardless.
consequence: Break into a shop at night in Steal mode and the empty shop SELLS to you at full price where DFU gives the shoplifting inventory; the computed open-shop latch is dead after entry.

title: Identify-SPELL commit tallies Mercantile and skips DFU's not-enough-magicka refusal
claim: commitTrade runs tallySkill(Mercantile, 1) unconditionally after every mode (worldModes.js:785), including the identifySpell arm (:772-779). DFU's identify-spell pass runs inside DoModeAction (DaggerfallTradeWindow.cs:957-995) and never reaches ConfirmTrade's TallySkill at :1088 - no tally for the spell (the paid service does tally, and the port matches there). DFU also refuses the whole pass when IdentifySpellCost > CurrentMagicka (:960-963); the port has no gate anywhere in the chain - commitTrade clamps Math.max(0, magicka - cost) (:775-777) and identifies everything anyway.
consequence: Every Identify cast trains Mercantile (accumulating skill-progress divergence), and a cast concluded with insufficient magicka still identifies all staged items where DFU refuses.

title: Quest ITEM stands take the NPC placement law; DFU's AddQuestItem never ground-rays
claim: standQuestFlatIn applies one law to NPCs and items: dungeon anchor `y - size.h/2` (the ITEM's own half-height) plus the AlignBillboardToGround raycast (worldModes.js:464-466); its comment asserts AddQuestNPC/AddQuestItem 'both call' the align (:457-459). AddQuestItem (GameObjectHelper.cs:1116-1160) never calls AlignBillboardToGround: its dungeon shift is the CONSTANT -randomTreasureMarkerDim/2 * GlobalScale = -0.5 (:1135-1136; DaggerfallLoot.cs:33, dim=40), then +Size.y/2, and the position stands with no ray. Only AddQuestNPC rays (:1040). standItem routes items through the same path with no distinction (worldModes.js:508-513, :576-580).
consequence: A dungeon quest item whose world-sprite height differs from 1.0 unit sits at a different height than DFU, and an item on an elevated marker (table, cage, ledge) is ray-snapped down to the surface below where DFU leaves it at the marker.

title: Quest-NPC ground ray originates at the BOTTOM anchor + 0.2; DFU rays from the CENTRE + 0.2
claim: AlignBillboardToGround casts from go.transform.position + 0.2 (GameObjectHelper.cs:340), and at that moment the position is the billboard CENTRE (interior: marker + Size.y/2 per :1034-1037; dungeon: the marker itself). The port rays from its bottom anchor `by + 0.2` (worldModes.js:465), half a sprite height LOWER in both site types. The on-hit landing formula agrees (bottom = hit + 0.02h), but the origin difference changes which floors the 4-unit ray finds: in a dungeon the port's origin (marker - h/2 + 0.2) can start at or below the floor for tall sprites.
consequence: Edge geometry only: a tall-sprite dungeon quest NPC can miss the floor snap DFU performs and stand embedded; floors near the 4-unit limit are found by one side and not the other.

title: commitTrade's 'Repair' arm has no caller and skips the UpdateRepairTimes queue law
claim: No call site opens the native trade window in 'Repair' mode (openTradeWindow is called with Buy/Sell/Identify/SellMagic only; openRepairService uses the keyed ChoiceWindow flow) - the arm at worldModes.js:755-765 is dead. If wired it diverges from DFU's ConfirmTrade Repair arm (DaggerfallTradeWindow.cs:1060-1072 -> UpdateRepairTimes(true) :514-568): it calls leaveForRepair with a bare per-item calculateItemRepairTime - no longest-job stretch, no never-decrease clamp - which the port's own keyed repairItem applies via updateRepairTimes (worldModes.js:1975-1984); its InstantRepairs branch also addItem()s an item never removed from the pack.
consequence: None reachable today (dead arm); a future wiring of the INVE12 native repair mode would silently skip the repair-queue law and duplicate instantly-repaired items.

title: bypassSavingThrows wrongly suppresses the magnitude-scaling saving throw
claim: Port: `saveScaled = spell.rangeType !== 0 && !ctx.bypassSavingThrows` gates effectMagnitude's savingThrow scaling (effects.js:437-441,577). DFU: AssignBundleFlags.BypassSavingThrows gates only the assign-time no-magnitude save (EntityEffectManager.cs:565-568) and reflection/resistance (:521,:525); GetMagnitude's ModifyEffectAmount runs for every non-CasterOnly bundle regardless of the flag (EntityEffect.cs:804-806), so bypassed casts of magnitude effects are still save-scaled per application in DFU. Reachable: quest spell-queue casts on foes - QuestResourceBehaviour.cs:346 assigns with BypassSavingThrows and the port mirrors it at questFoeHost.js:91 with bypassSavingThrows:true.
consequence: A quest-queued magnitude spell (Damage Health, Continuous Damage) lands at full magnitude every round in the port where DFU scales it by the foe's saving throw - quest foes take measurably more damage.

title: Soul Trap never rolls the target's no-magnitude saving throw
claim: DFU AssignBundle rolls FormulaHelper.SavingThrow for any effect with SupportMagnitude=false on a non-CasterOnly cast, dropping the whole effect on a full save (EEM:565-579). SoulTrap has SupportChance+SupportDuration, no magnitude, TargetFlags_Other, and does not set bypassSavingThrows (SoulTrap.cs:30-41; the bypass field's only writers are vampirism/lycanthropy/special effects). The port's soul-trap arm (effects.js:1278-1295) checks mobileType and rounds, then pushes/stacks with no savingThrow call - only the cast chance is forced true, which matches ChanceSuccess.
consequence: A monster with high willpower or Magic tolerance can never shrug off Soul Trap in the port; in DFU a full save drops the trap entirely - traps land strictly more often.

title: Pacify and Charm skip the no-magnitude saving throw
claim: PacifyEffect (SupportChance, no magnitude, TargetFlags_Other, PacifyEffect.cs:60-63) and CharmEffect (CharmEffect.cs:33-44) go through DFU's AssignBundle no-magnitude save (EEM:565-579) after the OnCast chance gate - the target can fully save and drop the effect. The port's arm (effects.js:1207-1216) does the group/class match and the dice100 chance roll only; no savingThrow is ever rolled for these kinds.
consequence: Pacify/Charm succeed more often in the port than in DFU against targets with Magic tolerance or high willpower - chance is the only gate instead of chance AND save.

title: Paralyze hard-immunity gate runs after reflection instead of before it
claim: DFU drops an incoming Paralyze for a hard-immune entity BEFORE the absorption/reflection/resistance chain (EEM:495-498 continue precedes the caster block at :504-527). The port tests isEntityImmuneToParalysis inside the isParalyze arm (effects.js:935), which runs AFTER the reflection gate (:672-679) and resistance gate (:685-691), so a hard-immune target with live Spell Reflection reflects a pure-Paralyze bundle back at the caster (out.reflected, re-applied by hosts at hostMagic.js:124-131 and world.js:1223-1225) where DFU silently discards the effect.
consequence: A player under Free Action (or a paralysis-immune career/race) with Spell Reflection up bounces a spider/wraith paralyze back at its caster; in DFU nothing happens. The resistance gate can also print 'Spell was resisted.' where DFU is silent.

title: Caster concealment break missing on Transfer/Drain/Paralyze/Silence arms
claim: DFU runs HandleAttackFromSource on the caster for these effects: TransferHealth/TransferFatigue via DamageHealthFromSource/DamageFatigueFromSource (DaggerfallEntityBehaviour.cs:143-169), and DrainEffect (:57), TransferEffect, Paralyze, Silence, DamageSpellPoints via PlayerAggro (EntityEffect.cs:815-828 -> HandleAttackFromSource :196-200), which breaks the caster's normal-power concealment. The port calls handleAttackFromSource only in the damageHealth/damageFatigue/damageSpellPoints/continuous arms; the transferHealth (effects.js:828-841), transferFatigue (:843-856), drain/transfer-attribute (:786-817), paralyze (:929-960) and buff/silence (:1297-1329) arms never call it.
consequence: An invisibility-normal or chameleon-normal player casting Paralyze, Silence, Transfer Health/Fatigue or a Drain at a foe keeps their concealment in the port; DFU breaks it when the cast lands.

title: seedBundleSeq has no caller - restored bundleIds collide with new casts
claim: effects.js:194-195 exports seedBundleSeq to lift the module-scope _bundleSeq past a restored save's high water mark, but grep of src/ finds zero callers. save.js persists bundleId (copyEffectEntry spreads whole entries, save.js:74-89, snapshot :155) and restores them (:303) without seeding, so after an app restart + load, _bundleSeq is 0 and the next cast reuses bundleId 1, colliding with the restored first cast's entries. liveBundles (mysticism.js:231-248) then merges two casts into one bundle and dispelBundle (mysticism.js:261-270, consumed at worldModes.js:3762) removes both. DFU has no counter to collide - bundles are object references re-instanced on load.
consequence: Cast a buff, save, restart the app, load, cast another spell: the HUD spell icons merge into one row and Dispel Magic on it strips both casts at once.

title: soulTrapNameSuffix is a ported function with no caller
claim: mysticism.js:379-385 ports ItemHelper.ResolveItemLongName's filled-trap suffix ('Soul Trap (Wraith)'), but grep of src/ finds no caller outside mysticism.js itself - no naming path appends it; only the info panel's %hs macro (itemInfo.js:190) surfaces the trapped soul.
consequence: A filled soul trap's item name never shows which soul it holds anywhere its name is printed; the player must open the info panel to tell full traps apart.

title: 'You are regenerating.' and 'You feel drained.' HUD lines never emitted
claim: DFU's Regenerate.Start prints youAreRegenerating for a player host (Regenerate.cs:48-52) and DrainEffect prints youFeelDrained on each magnitude increase when the host is the player (DrainEffect.cs:102-106); both strings verified in Internal_Strings.csv:638/642. The port's regenerate arm (effects.js:916-928) and drain/transfer arm (:786-817) call no sinks.say, and grep of src/ finds neither string anywhere, while the sibling concealment start texts and 'Spell was absorbed.' are wired.
consequence: The player gets no HUD feedback when a Regenerate lands on them or when a drain saps a stat, unlike DFU.

title: Create Item lastSelectedIndex is per-host instead of one static
claim: DFU's CreateItem.lastSelectedIndex is a single static shared across all casts in a run (CreateItem.cs:29,75,121). The port keeps two independent module-level copies - worldModes.js:189 and dungeonContext.js:137 - so the picker's remembered row does not carry between a dungeon cast and an overworld/interior cast.
consequence: Cast Create Item in a dungeon picking row N, exit, cast again outside: the picker opens at the exterior host's own remembered row (initially 0) instead of row N.

title: Class enemies get no enemy-group bit; DFU maps careerIndex (mobileType-128) into the monster table
claim: Port enemyGroupOf/entityFlags (:186, :206) look up ENEMY_GROUP_BIT[mobileType], so class enemies (>=128) get None; the comment at :194-198 claims that is DFU behaviour. It is not: GetEnemyEntityEnemyGroup switches on e.CareerIndex (FormulaHelper.cs:2752), and for EnemyClass careerIndex = ID-128 (EnemyEntity.cs:293), colliding into the MonsterCareers cases: Mage(0=Rat)=Animals, Burglar(7=Orc)=Humanoid, Barbarian(15)=Undead, Knight(17=Zombie)=Undead, CityWatch(18=Ghost)=Undead. PlayerGPS.GetEntityFlags:785-804, PacifyEffect.cs:132 and DispelUndead.cs:50-58 consume it with no class gate. Pin test/pacify.test.js:55-62 restates the port; port consumer effects.js:1212.
consequence: In DFU, Pacify Animal calms a class Mage, Pacify Undead calms a Knight/Barbarian/City Watch, Dispel Undead can destroy nearby Knights, and class enemies carry group bits in the nearby-object flags (Detect scans, Near-X enchantments). In the port none of these ever touch a class enemy.

title: Interior encounter table keyed by wrong BuildingTypes values
claim: Port BUILDING_TABLE (:36) maps {10:40, 11:41, 15:42, 17:42, 18:43, 19:44}, its comment claiming GuildHall=10, Temple=11, Palace=15. The port's own BUILDING_TYPES (world/buildingNames.js:18-24) matches DFLocation.cs:106-133: Library=10, GuildHall=11, Temple=14, Tavern=15, Palace=16. DFU routes GuildHall(11)->40, Temple(14)->41, Palace(16)||House1(17)->42, House2(18)->43, House3(19)->44, else 39. So the port sends Library to the guild-hall table, GuildHall to the temple table, Tavern to the palace table, and drops Temple/Palace to default 39. Latent: no caller in src/ passes ctx.buildingType yet (world.js:996, dungeonContext.js:966), and no test pins the map.
consequence: Once interior rest spawning is wired (DFU spawns via this exact path), resting in a Temple rolls the generic-house list, a Guild Hall rolls temple encounters, a Palace rolls house encounters, Taverns/Libraries roll tables classic never uses for them - wrong species spawn.

title: Classic-font key labels not uppercased; arrows named 'Left Arrow' instead of 'LEFT'
claim: The port's buttonText (:132-146) declares DFU's non-SDF classic-font arm as its law (header :23-24, :113-117) but never uppercases: DFU's GetButtonText ends 'return SDFFontRendering ? text : text.ToUpper()' (ControlsConfigManager.cs:521), so classic-font labels are all-caps. Arrows also diverge: DFU maps LeftArrow -> 'Left' (:474-479) -> 'LEFT'; the port maps ArrowLeft -> 'Left Arrow' (:141).
consequence: Controls-window key labels read 'Enter', 'Space', 'Left Arrow' in mixed case where DFU's classic-font window shows 'ENTER', 'SPACE', 'LEFT'; cosmetic only, no binding behavior differs.

title: Per-minute fatigue band is missing the climbing arm (22/min)
claim: DFU: amount = 11; if (climbingMotor.IsClimbing) amount = ClimbingFatigueLoss (22); else if running 88; else if swimming... (PlayerEntity.cs:405-413, constants :109-113). The port's band (worldTick.js:391-411) tests only activity.running then activity.swimming - no climbing test; no host passes a climbing flag into tickPlayerMinutes (world.js:1470, dungeonContext.js:2704 set only running/swimming/jumped), and FATIGUE_LOSS.Climbing = 22 (statMods.js:133) has zero consumers in src/ (grep: definition only).
consequence: A player climbing across a minute boundary pays 11 fatigue instead of 22 - half the classic climbing drain.

title: resetMagicRoundMarker never called: forward load fires up to 2880 spurious magic rounds
claim: DFU resets the broker's lastGameMinute on start AND load (InitMagicRoundTimer :817-823 'Called when game starts or loaded', plus LoadInProgress :206). The port's resetMagicRoundMarker (worldTick.js:608) has NO caller in src/. claimMagicRounds re-anchors only when the clock moved BACKWARDS (worldTick.js:119); its comment claims save.js re-anchors explicitly, but save.js:408 re-anchors only entity.lastGameMinutes, not the broker marker. worldQuickLoad (world.js:1654) sets the clock in-session with no marker reset, so a load to a LATER game time yields from = max(marker, to-2880) and a burst of up to 2880 rounds.
consequence: Loading a save ahead of the session clock instantly runs up to 2880 magic rounds: restored buffs expire on the spot, poisons burst, and a restored continuous-damage effect can kill on load.

title: 8-hour enemy-alert decay never runs in the dungeon hosts
claim: DFU lowers the alert 8 hours after raise inside PlayerEntity.Update (:381-384), every context. The port's decayEnemyAlert has ONE call site, createPlayerTicker.tick (shared.js:746) - pinned to exactly one by test/audit24_wave36.test.js:122-126 - but both dungeon hosts drive the clock via dungeonCtx.drawFoes -> tickPlayerMinutes directly (dungeonContext.js:2100; called from worldModes.js:2764 and dungeon.js:475), never through createPlayerTicker, and tickPlayerMinutes contains no decay. In a dungeon the alert clears only when a detecting foe dies (dungeonContext.js:1847).
consequence: Once any dungeon foe sees the player, the alert stays raised for the visit: the resting random-spawn roll keeps the alerted higher rate forever, where DFU relaxes it after 8 game hours.

title: Per-minute low-legal-rep guard-spawn arm unported from the catch-up loop
claim: DFU's per-minute catch-up loop (:486-518) also runs: if regionData[region].LegalRep < -10 && Dice100.SuccessRoll(5) then crimeCommitted = Criminal_Conspiracy; SpawnCityGuards(false) (:498-504). The port's copy (world.js:991-1017) runs only intermittentEnemySpawn; no legal-rep test exists anywhere in src/ (grep 'legalRep <' finds only court.js surrender/plea thresholds). The adjacent banished arm (:507-511) is FLAGGED pending in arrestFlow.js:159, but I found no flag covering the LegalRep < -10 arm.
consequence: A player with legal rep below -10 never has hunting city watch spawned per minute outdoors - the classic outlaw pressure loop is absent.

title: NPCSession's mobile arm has no caller; walker talk never sets the session target
claim: TalkManager.TalkToMobileNPC (:726-744) sets the mobile target: npcData rebuilt as Commoners of the region, alreadyRejectedOnce reset, numAnswersGivenTellMeAboutOrRumors zeroed. The port ports the arm (npcSession.js:439-455, :357-383) but nothing calls it: only talkToStaticNPC has callers (worldModes.js:978, :1365); the walker click runs townTalk.js's local path (:300-329) which never sets the session target. answerPipeline._session() (answerPipeline.js:289) reads npcSession.npcData for socialGroup/counters, so a walker conversation serves whatever the LAST static NPC left there.
consequence: Talking to a walker after any static NPC reuses that NPC's npcData - reaction tier's social-group modifier and the tell-me-about counter are the previous target's; the ported mobile-arm laws are dead code.

title: Exterior rain/crickets loop keeps sounding inside buildings and dungeons; DFU silences it
claim: The port never stops exterior ambience on interior/dungeon transition: world.js:3068-3086 and exterior.js:1426-1445 return on modal frames before ambience.setPreset/update (world.js:3280, exterior.js:1588), so the outdoor rain/crickets loop keeps looping indoors. ambientEffects.js:86-110 defends this as DFU bug-for-bug, but in DFU WeatherAmbientEffects is a child of the scene Exterior object (= PlayerEnterExit.ExteriorParent, fileID 1374841683), and TransitionInterior/DungeonInterior (PlayerEnterExit.cs:797/:931/:999) call DisableAllParents -> ExteriorParent.SetActive(false) (:1048), stopping its AudioSources; OnDisable (:96-100) clears the loop handles.
consequence: Enter a tavern or dungeon during rain (or crickets at night): the port keeps the outdoor loop audibly playing all visit; DFU goes silent when the Exterior parent deactivates.

title: Cemetery ambient layer (distant howl / creepy bird calls near graveyards) not implemented
claim: DFU has a second ambient channel for graveyards: cemeteryAmbientSounds = {AmbientDistantHowl(113), AmbientCreepyBirdCall(14) x2} (AmbientEffectsPlayer.cs:45-50), armed by OnEnterLocationRect when the location is a Graveyard and the player is outside (:518-529), ticking on its own Next(1,80)-second window (:154-162, :406-411, scene-serialized 1/80) and playing PlaySomewhereAround min distance 13 (:308-320). The port carries only the flag comment 'the cemetery howl/bird layer pends locations (routed)' (ambientEffects.js:33); grep of src/ finds no reference to indices 113/14, cemetery waits, or rect arming anywhere.
consequence: Standing in a graveyard exterior, DFU plays a howl or creepy bird call every 1-80 seconds; the port never plays any of the three clips, so graveyards sound like ordinary wilderness.

title: Dungeon water footstep hysteresis dropped: single 0.57 threshold vs DFU 0.57-enter/0.95-exit
claim: DFU enters shallow-water footsteps when (transform.y - 0.57) < waterY (PlayerFootsteps.cs:189) but resets water footsteps to stone only when (transform.y - 0.95) >= waterY or the water level clears (:199-208); between the thresholds the current water sound sticks. The port's pickFootstepSet is stateless (footsteps.js:49-50) and both dungeon hosts recompute dungeonShallow each frame with only the enter threshold (dungeon.js:414, worldModes.js:2679: (player.pos[1] + 0.9 - 0.57) < surf), so the port flips to stone 0.38 units earlier than DFU; same on leaving the submerged/swimming state.
consequence: Wading out of dungeon water, DFU keeps splash footsteps until the player has climbed a step higher; the port switches to stone footsteps early. Audible but brief.

title: Mobile street clicks bypass talkToMobileNPC - stale NPCData, one-answer gate never resets
claim: NPCSession.talkToMobileNPC (npcSession.js:439) has no caller in src/ (tests only). Both exterior hosts route mobile clicks through townTalk.activate (townTalk.js:274-329, from world.js:3175 / exterior.js:1514), which opens the engine-backed window (answers read npcSession.npcData via the pipeline) without calling setTargetMobileNPC/talkToNpc. C# TalkToMobileNPC (TalkManager.cs:727-745) builds a fresh NPCData and resets numAnswersGivenTellMeAboutOrRumors=0 every click (:742), and TalkToNpc runs ResetNPCKnowledge on a new target (:2652-2654). The port does neither on a mobile click: npcData keeps the last static NPC's socialGroup/race/isSpyMaster and answer counter.
consequence: After any conversation spends its one tell-me-about answer, every street NPC forever answers news/tell-me-about with the out-of-news/doesn't-know record; mobile answers also inherit the previous static NPC's social group and spymaster flag, and per-topic knowledge is never re-rolled.

title: buildingCompassDirection seam never wired - every engine %di answers '...never mind...'
