claim: AnswerPipeline.getKeySubjectLocationCompassDirection (answerPipeline.js:670) returns deps.buildingCompassDirection?.(key) ?? resolvingError, and the header (answerPipeline.js:67) claims TK-v wires it - but the only AnswerPipeline construction (world.js:2549-2587) omits buildingCompassDirection and no post-construction assignment exists. C# GetKeySubjectLocationCompassDirection (TalkManager.cs:1189-1201) calls GetBuildingCompassDirection (:1203-1235), computing the real 8-way direction from automap coordinates.
consequence: Every directional where-is answer through the native talk window expands %di to '...never mind...' ('The Bank is ...never mind... of here'); no NPC can ever give a direction, only the 35% map reveal works.

title: expandQuestTokens seam unwired for the pipeline - quest hints print raw tokens, never reveal
claim: _answerFromTokensArray (answerPipeline.js:653-658) returns deps.expandQuestTokens?.(questID, tokens) ?? tokens.map(t=>t.text??'').join(''). C# GetAnswerFromTokensArray (TalkManager.cs:3545-3559) always runs QuestMacroHelper.ExpandQuestMessage(quest, ref tokens, true) - expanding quest macros AND revealing dialog-linked resources - before TokensToString. world.js's AnswerPipeline deps (:2549-2587) never wire expandQuestTokens, while the RumorMill construction beside it does (world.js:2416-2431), so the omission is pipeline-only.
consequence: Every %hnt/%hnt2 tell-me-about answer for a quest topic prints with quest macros and symbol names unexpanded, and asking never reveals the topic's dialog-linked resources as C#'s reveal=true does.

title: TALK_MACROS omits %1com and other global talk macros - questions lose the PC greeting
claim: expandTalkMacros resolves an unknown macro to '' (talkMacros.js:228) and TALK_MACROS carries only 15 handlers - no %1com, %pcf, %pcn, %cn, %hnr, %ra. C#'s ExpandRandomTextRecord (TalkManager.cs:3580-3587) runs the FULL MacroHelper table: %1com -> GetPCGreetingOrFollowUpText (MacroHelper.cs:44, :957-960), %cn -> CityName (:567-573), %pcf/%pcn/%hnr/%ra all handled; unknown macros render 'sym[undefined]' (:527), not ''. Question records 7225+tone carry %1com and the answer set carries %cn/%pcf/%hnr/%ra (townTalk.js:509-524, talkSession.js:84-104 document both). getPCGreetingOrFollowUpText (answerPipeline.js:348) and getHonoric (:365) consequently have no caller in src/.
consequence: Every engine-path question drops the PC's opening greeting sentence (renders '. Where is ...'), the 7215-7223 greeting/follow-up/stranger machinery is dead code, and answer variants with %cn/%pcf/%hnr/%ra print those slots blank ('I'm new to  too.').

title: Static-NPC greetings expand no macros - npcSession's expandRandomTextRecord is a plain line join
claim: world.js wires NPCSession's expandRandomTextRecord as townTalk.lines(id).map(r=>r.text??r).join(' ') - no macro pass - while the AnswerPipeline below gets the real expandTalkRecord (world.js:2557). npcSession.talkToNpc (npcSession.js:529) draws the greeting (7206-7209 ladder or 8550-8571 guild table) through this seam. C# TalkToNpc (TalkManager.cs:2649) expands the greeting via ExpandRandomTextRecord, the full MacroHelper; the port's own greeting-set doc (talkSession.js:12-19) records these records carrying %pcf/%pcn/%cn/%oth.
consequence: Any static-NPC greeting variant carrying a macro shows the raw %-code on screen in every interior conversation opened through worldModes' static-NPC click; line joins also insert spaces where C# uses none.

title: computeTier discards questionType - reaction always gets the +5 where-is-building mod
claim: townTalk.computeTier (townTalk.js:434-441) does 'void questionType' and passes questionIndex: 0 into reactionTier012, so QUESTION_TYPE_REACTION_MODS[0] = +5 is added for every question. C# GetReactionToPlayer_0_1_2 (TalkManager.cs:663-667) uses GetClassicQuestionIndex(qt): +5 only for LocalBuilding/Regional (0) and QuestLocation/OrganizationInfo (4); Person(1), Work(3), QuestPerson(5), QuestItem(6) and News (default 2) get 0. The pipeline passes the real questionType through its reactionTier seam (answerPipeline.js:259, world.js:2585) and the host discards it.
consequence: When the first question of a tone in a session is Person/Work/News/QuestPerson/QuestItem, the NPC's reaction computes 5 points friendlier than DFU and the inflated value is cached for the session's tone - can shift the 0/1/2 answer-tone band.

title: questorGender read unconditionally - C# gates it to Work questions
claim: world.js wires talkMcp's questorGender as npcSession.getQuestorGender() unconditionally; C# GetMacroDataSource (TalkManagerMCP.cs:29-36) copies potentialQuestorGender only when the current question is Work AND HasNPCsWithWork, leaving the enum default Male otherwise, so %g..%g4 in a non-Work record always resolve male in C#.
consequence: A %g pronoun in a non-Work talk record would say 'she' when the standing selected questor is female where C# says 'he' - negligible since the pronoun macros live in the work answers.

title: clearSceneCache is ported but never called - interiors never forget, corpse-strip law dead
claim: DFU clears all non-permanent cached scenes on every map-pixel change (PlayerGPS.cs Update :331-339, 'Clear non-permanent scenes from cache, unless going to/from owned ship' -> SaveLoadManager.ClearSceneCache(false)) and on new game (StartGameBehaviour.cs:468). The port carries the whole law - clearSceneCache at sceneCache.js:110-130 including the permanent-scene 'sans corpses' filter (:124-127) - but NO file in src/ calls it (only tests; .audit26/unused.json lists it). worldModes.js only cacheScene (:1129) and restoreCachedScene (:1138); nothing expires entries on world movement.
consequence: Looted containers, emptied shelves and door states in every interior persist forever (DFU forgets them once the player leaves the map pixel); the permanent-scene corpse-strip never runs; and entity.sceneCache rides every save (save.js:123), so the quicksave grows with every interior ever exited.

title: undiscoverBuilding drops DFU's onlyIfResidence, TG/DB-hideout and matchName guards
claim: PlayerGPS.UndiscoverBuilding (:986-1019) refuses to undiscover when onlyIfResidence=true and the building is not a residence (:1005-1007), when its faction is Thieves Guild or Dark Brotherhood (:1009-1012), or when matchName differs from the stored displayName (:1014-1016). Its quest callers pass (buildingKey, true, buildingName) - TalkManager.cs:2958, Quest.cs:655. The port's undiscoverBuilding (discovery.js:66-68) deletes unconditionally, and no caller compensates: topicTree.js:432 forwards (buildingKey, buildingName) but world.js:2462 discards the name and checks nothing.
consequence: A quest siting a non-residence (tavern, shop, temple) erases it from the discovered-buildings store on topic-add/tombstone - gone from talk lists and the town map until re-discovered - and a residence whose name differs from the quest's is undiscovered where DFU keeps it; TG/DB hideouts lose their protection.

title: daedraSummonIndex/daedraSummonDay stored on the entity but missing from the save envelope
claim: DFU persists PlayerEntity.DaedraSummonDay and DaedraSummonIndex one-for-one (SerializablePlayer.cs:164-165 write, :332-333 restore). The port keeps the coven's remembered roll on playerEntity (daedraSummoning.js:109-111 mutates s.daedraSummonIndex/s.daedraSummonDay; worldModes.js:1635 passes state: playerEntity), but ENTITY_FIELDS (save.js:30-58) contains neither field and no other snapshotPlayer/restorePlayer line copies them, so a restored entity has both undefined and daedraSummoning.js:109's '!s.daedraSummonIndex' re-rolls.
consequence: The daedra a summoning-day coven answers with re-rolls on every fresh-session load instead of being pinned once per day - a player can reload to shop for the daedra prince they want, which DFU's persisted pair forbids.

title: weaponDrawn (and look/crouch state) not persisted; DFU restores sheath state on load
claim: SerializablePlayer.cs stores data.weaponDrawn = !weaponManager.Sheathed and usingLeftHand (:175-176) plus yaw/pitch/isCrouching in playerPosition (:212-214), and RestoreSaveData sets weaponManager.Sheathed = !data.weaponDrawn (:420-421). The port has live sheath state (combat/playerWeapon.js:78-88) but snapshotPlayer/restorePlayer (save.js:92-231, :260-410) and both hosts' envelopes (world.js:1624-1642) carry no weapon-drawn, yaw/pitch or crouch fields.
consequence: Continuing a save in a fresh session always comes back with the weapon sheathed and a default view direction even if the game was saved mid-fight with the weapon drawn; DFU restores both.

title: Notebook restore substitutes an empty block where DFU leaves the live notebook standing
claim: DFU only restores the notebook when the save actually carries NotebookData ('if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(notebookDataJson))', SaveLoadManager.cs:1451-1456); with no block the session's live notes stand. The port's questBridge restore (questBridge.js:348) calls notebook.restoreSaveData(data.notebook ?? { notebookEntries: [], finishedQuestEntries: [] }), and PlayerNotebook.restoreSaveData (notebook.js:205-208) replaces both lists - so a quest envelope without a notebook field wipes them.
consequence: Loading a save whose quest envelope predates the notebook field erases every note and filed quest made this session, where DFU's guarded arm keeps them; only affects old-version saves.

title: Court fine clamp reads coins only where DFU reads gold + letters of credit
claim: startCourt clamps the fine with `const gold = goldAmount(player)` (court.js:284; goldAmount at :151-153 counts only the Currency stack), converting any shortfall to prison days at :285-288. DFU's state-0 court uses `playerEntity.GetGoldAmount()` (DaggerfallCourtWindow.cs:169), which is goldPieces + letters of credit (PlayerEntity.cs:1313-1316). The port's own totalGoldAmount (court.js:163-165) is the exact mirror of GetGoldAmount and is not used here, while pleaGuilty later charges the fine through deductGold, which DOES spend letters (court.js:199-225).
consequence: A defendant carrying wealth as letters of credit (e.g. 10 coins + a 5000-gold letter, fine 400) has the fine cut to 10 and serves ~9 extra prison days; DFU charges the full 400 and adds no days.

title: Bank repay/purchase gates use coins-only gold where DFU uses GetGoldAmount
claim: repayLoan adds `player.gold()` to the repayable pool (banking.js:488), and purchaseHouse (:221-223) and purchaseShip (:301) gate on `player.gold() + accountGold`. The live purse seam wires gold() to coins-only goldAmount (scenes/worldModes.js:1278, bankPurse). DFU's RepayLoan (DaggerfallBankManager.cs:513-516), PurchaseHouse (:415-418) and PurchaseShip (:474-477) all read playerEntity.GetGoldAmount() = goldPieces + letters of credit (PlayerEntity.cs:1313-1316). Coins-only IS correct for depositGold/withdrawGold (DFU uses GoldPieces there), so the one seam conflates two DFU quantities; past the gate the port pays via deductGold, which spends letters, so gate and payment disagree.
consequence: With a short coin purse but letters covering the price, the bank answers NOT_ENOUGH_GOLD for a loan repayment, house purchase, or ship purchase that DFU accepts.

title: Tavern room and food gold gates are coins-only; DFU accepts letters of credit
claim: _confirm refuses the room when `goldAmount(h.entity) < d.price` (tavernWindow.js:194; goldAmount from court.js counts coins only), and _food passes `gold: goldAmount(h.entity)` into eatOrDrink's poor-check (:223, tavern.js:191). DFU gates both on GetGoldAmount() - coins plus letters of credit - at DaggerfallTavernWindow.cs:218 and :324, then deducts via DeductGoldAmount, which spends letters. The port also pays via deductGold (:195, :226), which spends letters, so only the gate diverges.
consequence: A player holding letters of credit but few coins is refused a room rental or a meal that DFU sells them (and that the port itself could charge once past the gate).

title: Region-condition store never minted at new game - PricesHigh/Low arms dead until first load
claim: createRegionConditions' only caller is restoreRegionConditions (regionConditions.js:188), reached only from save restore (save.js:395); no new-game path assigns entity.regionConditions (no other assignment exists in src/). worldTick passes `entity.regionConditions ?? null` (worldTick.js:253) and updateRegionalPrices skips the flag half on null (shopStock.js:309). DFU mints regionData at every new game (StartGameBehaviour.cs:433 -> InitializeRegionData, PlayerEntity.cs:2189-2211), so FormulaHelper.cs:2075-2087 writes PricesHigh/PricesLow from day one. save.js:392-394 even assumes a blank store 'is what InitializeRegionData mints at a new game anyway' - but nothing mints it.
consequence: In a session started fresh (no load), the shipped PricesHigh/PricesLow condition writes never execute and the first save records a blank condition store, diverging from DFU's save-relevant regionData flag state.

title: New-game 12-pass faction power bootstrap has no caller
claim: DFU's InitializeRegionData ends with 12 iterations of RegionPowerAndConditionsUpdate(false) then (true) (PlayerEntity.cs:2213-2217), giving every rumor-mill faction 24 power-walk steps (plus child bonuses) before play begins. The port's regionPowerUpdate has exactly two callers, worldTick.js:491 and :508 (the 7- and 38-day arms); nothing runs it at character creation (attachFactionRep, factionRep.js:204-220, only builds the store and applies biography rep). regionConditions.js:92-95 defers the bootstrap to 'the update itself, which is the next slice', but that slice (S43, regionPower.js) shipped without it; its FLAGGED note covers only the unported conditions half, not the power bootstrap.
consequence: A fresh character starts with raw FACTION.TXT powers instead of DFU's 24-step-walked start state, shifting the merchants-vs-region term of every UpdateRegionalPrices day and all later power reads for the whole save.

title: Biography 'GP -N' subtracts gold where DFU's signed parse makes it ADD
claim: In BiogFile.ApplyPlayerEffect, int.TryParse(tokens[1]) on "-500" yields parseResult = -500, and the '-' branch runs `playerEntity.GoldPieces -= parseResult;` (BiogFile.cs:287) - a double negative that INCREASES gold by 500 (the :289 clamp never fires). The port at biography.js:121 does `stack.stackCount = Math.max(0, stack.stackCount - Math.abs(v))` - it actually subtracts and floors at 0. test/biography.test.js:85-87 pins the port's subtract-and-clamp while citing the C# clamp comment - the pin restates the port, not DFU.
consequence: A BIOG answer with a GP - effect leaves the player poorer than DFU (port removes N, DFU adds N). No shipping BIOG file carries a '-' GP line (all 55 are '+'), so only custom/modified biographies hit it.

title: runInfections advances only the FIRST live infection; DFU ticks every infection bundle each round
claim: runInfections (infection.js:298-314) calls liveInfection (infection.js:195-196), a `.find(...)` returning only the first non-ended infection, and steps only that entry per round. The port allows vampirism and lycanthropy infections live at once (infectionAccepted, infection.js:169-175, blocks only same-key and the opposing strain; test/infection.test.js:119-121 pins 'four days from two different fates at once'). In DFU, DoMagicRound iterates ALL instanced bundles and calls MagicRound() on every live effect (EntityEffectManager.cs:1724-1734), so VampirismInfection.ProgressDisease (:99-103) and LycanthropyInfection.ProgressDisease (:82-86) each run every round independently.
consequence: A player carrying both infections sees only the earlier one progress: the second's warning dream and 3-day turn stall until the first deploys or is cured, then fire late - DFU runs both lifecycles on schedule in parallel.

title: Guild rank law reads live (enchant-modded) skill, DFU reads GetPermanentSkillValue
claim: Guild.CalculateNumHighLowSkills (Guild.cs:124) reads GetPermanentSkillValue, which excludes effect mods (DaggerfallSkills.cs:135-143 vs 176). The port's numHighLowSkills (guilds.js:202) calls skillValue (skills.js:60-71), which adds entity._enchantMods.skillMods[skillId] (skills.js:68) - the port's live mods channel, populated when the player equips an EnhancesSkill item (enchantments.js:655; DFU EnhancesSkill.cs:78 writes SetSkillMod, live-only). The file's own header (guilds.js:22-24) claims permanent reads. Feeds calculateNewRank, updateRank and isEligibleToJoin.
consequence: A player wearing an EnhancesSkill (+15) item on a guild skill can join or be promoted on skills their permanent values don't earn (and demoted on unequip); in DFU worn enchantments never move guild rank.

title: Training 'too skilled' gate compares live skill, DFU compares permanent
claim: TrainingSkill_OnItemPicked refuses training when GetPermanentSkillValue(skillToTrain) > GetTrainingMax (DaggerfallGuildServiceTraining.cs:101). The port's tooSkilledToTrain (guildServiceActions.js:108) uses skillValue(entity, skill), which folds entity._enchantMods.skillMods (skills.js:68), i.e. the live value including worn EnhancesSkill enchantments.
consequence: A player with permanent skill 40-50 wearing a +15 EnhancesSkill item is refused with 4022 ('too skilled') where DFU trains them; the 50-cap check moves with equipment.

title: Witches coven constants wrong: type 6 should be 8, guild group 8 should be 22
claim: daedraSummoning.js:70-71 defines WITCHES_COVEN_TYPE = 6 and WITCHES_GUILD_GROUP = 8, commented as DFU's WitchesCoven/Witches. FactionFile.cs has WitchesCoven = 8 (6 is VampireClan) and Witches = 22 (8 is GGroup8); the port's own factionFile.js:18,34 agrees. The caller (worldModes.js:1631,1650) passes the raw record's type/ggroup, so a real coven fails both tests: daedraForSummoner:104 skips the coven random-prince branch (DaggerfallQuestPopupWindow.cs:180-189) and attemptSummoning:166 never sets spawnFoes (cs:256). The pins use the constants symbolically, restating the port.
consequence: When the coven service lands (route currently flagged to talk), covens summon only on the 16 calendar days instead of a daily random non-Hircine prince, and failed coven summonings never mark the daedric-foe reprisal.

title: Cure-disease price skips the regional price adjustment DFU always applies
claim: DFU computes costBeforeBargaining = FormulaHelper.CalculateCost(baseCost, quality) (cs:85), and CalculateCost unconditionally runs ApplyRegionalPriceAdjustment (FormulaHelper.cs:1895, 2026-2044), scaling by the region's PriceAdjustment (750-1250). The port calls calculateCost(baseCost, quality) (guildServiceActions.js:215) whose third priceAdjustment parameter defaults to neutral 1000 (shopStock.js:325-328); the comment misreads the two-arg C# call - the omitted third parameter is conditionPercentage, not the regional term. The port models regional prices elsewhere (tradeModes.js:242) but never passes them here.
consequence: Temple curing costs the same in every province; in DFU the quote varies up to about +/-25% with the region's price adjustment.

title: Knightly rank-9 promotion never consults house ownership; blocking flag is stale
claim: KnightlyOrder.GetPromotionMsgId rank 9 returns DaggerfallBankManager.OwnsHouse ? 5241 : 5240 (KnightlyOrder.cs:144-145; OwnsHouse is per-current-region, DaggerfallBankManager.cs:136). The port's static promotionByRank maps 9 -> 5240 unconditionally (guildVariants.js:200) behind a comment saying 'Banking does not exist yet' - but banking's ownsHouse landed (systems/banking.js:167) and is consumed in the same host that shows promotions (worldModes.js:1694); promotionTextId (guilds.js:280-298) has no ownsHouse seam.
consequence: A knight promoted to rank 9 while owning a house in the region is shown record 5240 instead of DFU's 5241 - the wrong promotion speech.

title: Non-member at knightly seneschal gets rank refusal 460 instead of members-only line
claim: In DFU a non-member (or member of a different order) at a knightly hall gets guildNotMember (GuildManager.cs:246), whose CanAccessService(ReceiveHouse) falls to Guild.cs's base default false, so DoGuildService shows 'My services are reserved for members only.' (GuildServicePopupWindow.cs:314-326). The port applies the order's own switch to everyone: knightlyCanAccessService answers ReceiveHouse -> true unconditionally (guildServices.js:268), serviceAccess allows it (worldModes.js:1430), and receiveHouseDecision then refuses with TEXT.RSC 460 (knightlyGifts.js:120) - the record DFU reserves for members below rank 9.
consequence: Any non-member clicking a knightly order seneschal sees the rank-9 refusal text instead of DFU's members-only line - reachable, player-visible wrong message.

title: Already-given-house line diverges from DFU's localized string
claim: KnightlyOrder.ReceiveHouse shows GetLocalizedText("serviceReceiveHouseAlready") (KnightlyOrder.cs:230), which the clone's Internal_Strings_en table renders as 'You have already received your house.' The port's ALREADY_GIVEN_HOUSE (knightlyGifts.js:93, shown via worldModes.js:1700-1702) is 'You have already been given a house.'
consequence: A rank-9 knight reclaiming the house gift reads a different sentence than DFU shows; text-only divergence.

title: Stendarr AvoidDeath benefit missing entirely - no port counterpart, no flag
claim: Temple.AvoidDeath (Temple.cs:450-460) gives a Stendarr member a Random.Range(0,50) < rank chance, when not submerged, to survive a killing blow; PlayerEntity.SetHealth (PlayerEntity.cs:1205-1211) then restores 10% MaxHealth instead of raising OnDeath, via GuildManager.AvoidDeath (GuildManager.cs:396-402). guildServices.js carries every other benefit override (canRest, hallAccessAnytime, freeHealing, freeMagickaRecharge, freeTavernRooms, freeShipTravel, reduced costs; DeepBreath in breath.js) but has no avoidDeath, and grep of src/, test/ and bible/ finds no equivalent or FLAG anywhere, including the death path (systems/playerDeath.js, statMods.js kill seams).
consequence: A Stendarr temple member dies outright on any killing blow; in DFU a rank-r member survives at 10% health with probability r/50 - a whole guild benefit a player can hit is absent.

title: ItemDeteriorates params shifted: DFU 0=AllTheTime/1=Sunlight/2=Holy, port 0=sunlight/1=holy/2=always
claim: DFU's Params enum is AllTheTime=0, InSunlight=1, InHolyPlaces=2, and MagicRound returns early only when (param==InSunlight && !inSunlight) || (param==InHolyPlaces && !inHolyPlace) — param 0 degrades unconditionally. The port's magicRound gates `param === 0` on ctx.inSunlight and `param === 1` on ctx.inHolyPlace, so param 2 falls through both ifs and degrades unconditionally. The port's own catalogue (enchantmentCatalogue.js:80,251,259) uses the correct DFU order (labels 0='all the time', 1='in sunlight', 2='in holy places'; Daedroth/FrostDaedra/Ghost/Wraith souls force param 2 = InHolyPlaces), so the two port modules disagree with each other as well as with the C#.
consequence: A soul-bound item carrying ItemDeteriorates InHolyPlaces (param 2) loses 1 condition every 4 magic rounds everywhere and is eventually consumed; an all-the-time (param 0) drawback never fires; sunlight (param 1) items idle on the holy-place seam.

title: HealthLeech params shifted: DFU 0=WheneverUsed/1=Daily/2=Weekly, port 2=WheneverUsed/0=Daily/1=Weekly
claim: DFU's Params enum is WheneverUsed=0, UnlessUsedDaily=1, UnlessUsedWeekly=2: the use/strike bill (16/8 hp) fires at param 0 (:86), the idle drain at params 1 (day) and 2 (week). The port's used/strikes handlers bill at `param === 2` and its magicRound treats 0 as daily and 1 as weekly. The catalogue (enchantmentCatalogue.js:77,253: labels 0='Whenever used', DaedraSeducer forces param 2 = UnlessUsedWeekly) uses the correct DFU order, so port modules also disagree with each other. test/enchantments.test.js:62 (`item(T.HealthLeech, 2) // WheneverUsed`) and :103 (param 0 as daily) pin the port's wrong mapping while citing HealthLeech.cs — the pin restates the port.
consequence: A Daedra-Seducer-bound item (weekly leech in DFU) bills the wearer 16 hp per use / 8 per strike; a classic WheneverUsed (param 0) item instead drains 1 hp per 4 rounds after a day idle and never bills on use.

title: Enchanted payload never dispatched: FeatherWeight/ExtraWeight/HealthLeech maker arms are dead code
claim: DFU's SetEnchantments fires EnchantmentPayloadCallback(Enchanted) per enchantment carrying the flag (:1298-1300) and unequips the item (:1341). The port's applyEnchantments (enchanting.js:200-206) only copies the list, ui/itemMakerWindow.js:285 calls it with no payload dispatch, and no caller anywhere in src/ passes PAYLOAD.Enchanted to doItemEnchantmentPayloads — the registry's enchanted() handlers (enchantments.js:424-425) and HealthLeech's Enchanted stamp arm can never run, and SoulBound's trap consumption has no path either.
consequence: Feather Weight leaves the item's weight unchanged (DFU sets 0.25kg); Extra Weight never quadruples it; a fresh daily/weekly HealthLeech item starts at stamp 0 and leeches immediately; the item stays equipped where DFU force-unequips.

title: Recipe picker part-fills the cauldron; DFU refuses on any missing ingredient and clears first
claim: DFU's AddRecipeToCauldron builds a dict of required ingredients and, if ANY is unmatched, shows 'reqIngredients' and moves NOTHING (:298-300); only with all present does it ClearCauldron() (:304) then add the full set. The port's gatherRecipe comment claims DFU 'fills what it can... does not refuse the whole recipe for one missing herb', and the caller (ui/potionMakerWindow.js:184-194) adds the found subset on top of existing cauldron contents with no message and no clear. test/potions.test.js:179-188 pins the partial fill while citing the same C# lines — the pin restates the port, not the C#.
consequence: Picking a known recipe while missing one herb silently loads a partial cauldron; Mix then fails and consumes the herbs where DFU would have refused with a message and consumed nothing. Residual cauldron contents also pollute a fill instead of being cleared.

title: WeakensArmor applies +5 armor in port but is a no-op in DFU (setter guard refuses positive values)
claim: WeakensArmor's ConstantEffect calls SetDecreasedArmorValueModifier(5), but that setter (DaggerfallEntity.cs:410-416) assigns only when `amount < DecreasedArmorValueModifier`, and the modifier is cleared to 0 every DoConstantEffects pass (ClearConstantEffects, DaggerfallEntity.cs:842) — 5 < 0 is never true, so the +5 never lands and the enchantment is inert in DFU. The port's row adds WEAKENS_ARMOR_VALUE (+5) into mods.armorMod each round, which combat/formulas.js:292 adds to the wearer's armor value in the attacker's hit chance.
consequence: In the port a WeakensArmor side effect makes the wearer 5 points easier to hit; in DFU it does nothing — the drawback the player took for -700 budget costs defense only in the port.

title: Armor modifiers stack additively per item in port; DFU's setters are non-stacking min-sets
claim: DFU's SetIncreasedArmorValueModifier keeps only the lowest value ('does not stack'), so any number of StrengthensArmor items (each setting -5 via StrengthensArmor.cs:63) yields exactly -5; BadReactionsFrom's SetDecreasedArmorValueModifier(-5) likewise floors at -5 across items (its ChanceToHitModifier IS additive, DaggerfallEntity.cs:418-421). The port folds these into one additive channel: each StrengthensArmor row does `mods.armorMod += -5` (enchantments.js:428) and each active BadReactionsFrom adds another -5 (:527), so two Strengthens items give -10 where DFU caps at -5.
consequence: Wearing two or more StrengthensArmor items (or multiple active BadReactionsFrom items) makes the port player measurably harder to hit than DFU allows — -5 per item instead of a -5 channel cap.

title: Enchantment cap off-by-one: DFU's `++count > 10` break applies 11, port slices at 10
claim: SetEnchantments increments count AFTER adding each enchantment and breaks only when `++count > maxEnchantments` (10) — the break fires after the 11th add, so an oversized list keeps 11 enchantments. The port's applyEnchantments does `enchantments.slice(0, MAX_ENCHANTMENTS)` (10), and its comment says 'DFU applies the first ten'. The port's own openPickerDecision comment notes forced enchantments can push the lists past the ==10 picker guard, so 11+ lists are reachable.
consequence: An 11-enchantment item (e.g. via SoulBound's forced children crossing the ==10 guard) silently loses its 11th enchantment in the port; DFU keeps it.

title: Book arm lacks DFU's !IsArtifact guard
claim: DFU's book arm is `item.ItemGroup == ItemGroups.Books && !item.IsArtifact` — artifact books (Oghma Infinium) skip the reader and fall through to the enchanted Used payload at the tail. The port's isBook (useItem.js:80) tests group only, so an artifact book answers {kind:'book'} and opens the reader before the payload.
consequence: When artifact items exist in the port, using the Oghma Infinium opens the plain book reader instead of only firing its artifact payload; low reachability today since artifact effect classes pend.

title: CastWhenHeld wear runs for non-player wearers; DFU's MagicRound payload is player-only
claim: DFU dispatches the MagicRound item payload only for items in activeMagicItemsInRound, populated solely under `if (IsPlayerEntity)` (:1744-1752) — an enemy's Cast-When-Held item never takes the 1-per-4-rounds wear. The port's pump (worldTick.js:160, 'every host's player AND foes get it') calls enchantmentMagicRound for foes too, and CastWhenHeld's magicRound (enchantments.js:316-319) has no player gate, so an enemy's held item degrades and is consumed on break via enchantLowerCondition. (Bundle-driven rounds — RegensHealth, ItemDeteriorates, HealthLeech idle — do run for any entity in DFU, so those are correctly ungated.)
consequence: An enemy wearing a Cast-When-Held magic item has it wear out and vanish over time in the port; in DFU it survives to be looted at its remaining condition.

title: createArtifact never marks the artifact identified (DFU sets identifiedMask at mint)
claim: DFU SetArtifact writes `flags = artifactMask | identifiedMask` (DaggerfallUnityItem.cs:617) so every artifact is born identified. The port's createArtifact (loot.js:280-295) sets artifact/magic/enchantments but never isIdentified, and no other producer does (only shopStock.js:484 and worldModes.js:774/782 write isIdentified). itemIsIdentified (tradeModes.js:130) requires isIdentified===true for any enchanted item, so every artifact reads UNIDENTIFIED.
consequence: expandItemInfo (itemInfo.js:186-189) drops an unidentified item's own name, so an artifact's info panel shows the base template name instead of the artifact name; the Identify service stages an artifact and charges (25*value)>>8 (tradeModes.js:244-251, 363) where DFU refuses (DaggerfallTradeWindow.cs:823-826).

title: Equip-swap pause billed per hand transition; DFU bills only the net change per inventory-window session
claim: DFU snapshots the hand items at inventory OnPush (SetEquipDelayTime(false), DaggerfallInventoryWindow.cs:667) and bills once at OnPop (:729): only `if (lastRightHandItem != currentRightHandItem)` adds delay(last)+delay(current) (:1164-1183). The port's billEquipDelay (equip.js:52-58) fires inside unequipSlot (:67) and equipItem (:190) on EVERY transition; its comment claims 'each transition exactly once' is the DFU law. test/ch3.test.js:77 pins the accumulating behavior - the pin restates the port; its single-swap case happens to match DFU.
consequence: Multiple equips in one inventory visit over-bill the attack-block countdown: dagger then katana from empty hands bills 500+500+3400 where DFU bills 3400; unequip and re-equip the same weapon bills 2x its delay where DFU bills zero. The weapon is blocked longer than classic after any multi-step swap.

title: Alchemist shelf never rolls the 25% potion recipe though the ported helper ships in loot.js
claim: DFU StockShopShelf's Alchemist arm calls RandomlyAddPotionRecipe(25, items) (DaggerfallLoot.cs:163-166). The port's Alchemist branch is a comment only (shopStock.js:150-152, 'potion recipes pend (loud)'), but the stated blocker no longer exists: loot.js:383-389 ships randomlyAddPotionRecipe verbatim (CLASSIC_RECIPE_KEYS, template 278), already consumed by addEnemyLootExtras (loot.js:404) and addPileLootExtras (loot.js:423), and shopStock.js already imports createRandomPotion from the same module (line 108).
consequence: Alchemist shop shelves never stock a potion recipe (25% chance per restock in DFU/classic), removing the main legitimate purchase source of recipes.

title: Shop shelves skip the MagicItems group; Pawn Shops never stock random magic items
claim: DFU's shelf loop creates CreateRandomMagicItem for the MagicItems group (DaggerfallLoot.cs:240-243); itemGroupsPawnShop carries pair 0x04,0x0A (DaggerfallLootDataTables.cs:61) so pawn shops stock magic items at chanceMod 10. The port hard-skips: `if (group === 'MagicItems') continue; // INTERIM loud` (shopStock.js:166), yet the same file already mints real magic items via createRegularMagicItem for the guild shelf (shopStock.js:483) and loot.js exposes the MAGIC.DEF registry via getMagicItemTemplates() (loot.js:302).
consequence: Pawn shop shelves never show a random enchanted item (in DFU each MagicItems template rolls Dice100 under 10*5*(21-rarity)/100 when rarity <= quality), closing a classic source of purchasable magic items.

title: Repair days label uses committed time, not the queue-stretched estimate, for in-repair items
claim: DFU's label calls item.RepairData.EstimatedDaysUntilRepaired() (DaggerfallTradeWindow.cs:283-288), reading timeStarted + EstimatedRepairTime (ItemRepairData.cs:36-42) - the value the estimate pass just recomputed with the longest-job stretch and never-decrease clamp (DaggerfallTradeWindow.cs:548, 556, 566). The port's repairStatusLabel (repairService.js:156-163) uses repairTimeDone(item) = timeStarted + committed repairTime for any in-repair item, ignoring its estimateMinutes parameter in that branch.
consequence: When an in-repair item is the longest job and more items are staged beside it, DFU shows the new stretched estimate (e.g. '4 days') while the port shows the old committed '3 days' until the trade confirms - a transient label divergence.

title: Daedric quest offer crashes: _offerQuest dereferences this._guild which offerNamedQuest set to null
claim: offerNamedQuest (offerFlow.js:129-139) sets this._guild = null, then on a loaded quest calls _offerQuest(), which runs `if (this._guild.isMember())` (offerFlow.js:199) with no null guard - TypeError. In DFU the guild ExternalMCP assignment exists only in DaggerfallGuildServicePopupWindow.OfferQuest (:608) where guild is always non-null; the daedra path (DaggerfallQuestPopupWindow.cs:272-279) never touches a guild - DaggerfallDaedraSummonedWindow.cs:96-121 shows the offer. Live caller: worldModes.js:1675 -> offerDaedricQuest -> offerNamedQuest; daedra quest sources are vendored (vendor/dfu-quests/Quests/X0C00Y00.txt), so getQuest returns non-null and the crash line is reached.
consequence: First-time successful daedra summoning throws a TypeError instead of presenting the daedric quest offer; the quest can never be offered or accepted (gold already spent, Summoned flag already set).

title: expandLetterSignoff is ported but has no caller in src/ - quest letters never get their 'Letter: ...' name
claim: questMacros.js:492 ports ExpandLetterSignoff whole (its comment says the inventory arc's parchment label rides it), but grep of src/ finds zero callers - only test/questmacros.test.js uses it. In DFU, ItemHelper.ResolveItemLongName's quest-letter arm (ItemHelper.cs:335-348) calls ExpandLetterSignoff for any Parchment quest item. The port's item label maker (worldModes.js:633 _itemLabel) answers name ?? template name and never routes parchments through the signoff.
consequence: Quest letters in inventory show the generic parchment/template name instead of DFU's 'Letter: <signoff>'; multiple quest letters are indistinguishable. (Possible refutation: item.js:86-92 documents plain-template-name labels as the port's current one-convention.)

title: Villager pick sets raceIx = RACES.indexOf('Human') = -1; design skin tone never applies
claim: applyVillagerTone (lines 439-447) does raceIx = RACES.indexOf('Human'), but RACES (line 361) is now eight real races with no 'Human' entry (the four-family era it belonged to is described at lines 357-360). PALETTES.human entries do carry names 'Pale'/'Fair'/'Deep' (src/characters/palettes.js:7-12) and every villager ships a tone via RACE_TONE (villagerDesigns.js:296-299, attached at paperdollPayload.js:319), so ti>=0 and raceIx becomes -1 on every villager selection. applyTone (603-604) reads RACES[-1]=undefined and bails at `if (!pal) return`; loadHeads/loadFaceSet get an undefined race and silently drop; toneIx.Human is a key no reader uses (toneIx built from RACES at 602).
consequence: Picking any villager in the shipped viewer silently discards the design's authored skin tone (a Redguard renders default-toned instead of 'Deep'), head/face sets stop loading, and the race/tone controls run off raceIx=-1 until the race button is clicked. A shipped law thrown away at the seam.

title: Viewer gesture gate uses net displacement + full reset, not DFU's TravelDist rolling window
claim: The viewer's local drag-to-swing (lines 1184-1194), commented 'verbatim mechanics' (1168), gates on Math.hypot(gest.x, gest.y)/longest >= ATTACK_THRESHOLD (net summed vector) and zeroes the whole gesture once its start exceeds MAX_GESTURE_SECONDS (1186). DFU gates on Gesture.TravelDist/_longestDim (WeaponManager.cs:808), the summed per-delta path length, documented as not equal to the sum's magnitude 'because the trail may bend' (WeaponManager.cs:99-101), and TrimOld (111-122) is a rolling per-point 1s window, not a reset. The port's game path already does this right after AUDIT 24 (src/combat/playerWeapon.js:118-160); only the viewer retains the collapsed version.
consequence: On the dev viewer page, curved/zig-zag drags need far more motion to fire a strike than in DFU or the port's own game, and a drag crossing 1s loses all accumulated travel at once — the bench misrepresents the swing feel it exists to demonstrate. Dev-tool only; no player-facing effect.

title: Guild service popup paints opaque black backdrop; DFU sets ParentPanel to Color.clear
claim: guildServiceWindow.js:172 calls drawMenuBackdrop (MENU_BACKDROP = [0,0,0,1], chargenArt.js:58) citing DaggerfallBaseWindow's black default, but this window's own constructor overrides it: 'ParentPanel.BackgroundColor = Color.clear;' (DaggerfallGuildServicePopupWindow.cs:99; ScreenDimColor is also hardwired clear, DaggerfallPopupWindow.cs:27,34) - in DFU the scene stays visible around the 130x51 popup. Same defect class AUDIT 24 fixed for 5 other windows (test/startwindow.test.js:483-525 lists charsheet/talk/trade/inventory/journal); the guild popup was missed and no test pins the black.
consequence: Clicking a guild/temple service NPC blacks out the whole screen behind the small panel; in DFU the room stays visible behind it.

title: Bank purchase panel drawn at y=50; DFU's Middle alignment overrides Position to y=35.5
claim: The port sets PURCHASE_PANEL_Y = 50 from 'mainPanel.Position (:124) is (0, 50) under a MIDDLE alignment' (bankPurchaseWindow.js:40-41). In DFU, VerticalAlignment.Middle ignores position.y: BaseScreenComponent.cs:1234-1236 centers the rect, so the 225x129 panel (DaggerfallBankPurchasePopUp.cs:122-126 sets Center/Middle AND Position(0,50)) sits at y=35.5. The port's own guildServiceWindow.js:10-16 documents this exact law ('BOTH alignments ignore Position'); bankPurchaseWindow missed it. Hits shift with the panel so the window is self-consistent, just placed low.
consequence: The house-purchase window renders ~15 native pixels lower on screen than DFU/classic.

title: BUY keeps the purchase list open on a failed purchase; DFU closes it unconditionally
claim: DFU's BuyButton_OnMouseClick calls CloseWindow() BEFORE GeneratePurchaseHousePopup (DaggerfallBankPurchasePopUp.cs:386-390): the list closes regardless of result and the result box shows over the banking window. The port's _buy (bankPurchaseWindow.js:122-135) shows the box over the still-open purchase window and _dismissBox (:137-143) closes only on PURCHASED_HOUSE. Also DFU plays ButtonClick before the SelectedIndex<0 guard (:382-383); the port after it (:123-126).
consequence: After a refused purchase (e.g. not enough gold) the port leaves the player in the purchase list; DFU returns them to the bank window.

title: Nameplate pair-fallback arms conjoin checks DFU applies sequentially, skipping DFU's place-one-alone path
claim: DFU's easy-pair fallback shifts FIRST by 2x bias and places it whenever first's own check passes, then places second only if clear at zero (ExteriorAutomap.cs:1230-1240; symmetric :1242-1252); whenever first is placed, second.numCollisionsDetected-- (:1274-1275), which can drop second to 0 so the next zero pass (:1317-1318) places second at its ORIGINAL spot. The port (nameplateLayout.js:81-87) conjoins clearOfPlaced(p,2x) AND clearOfPlaced(q,0) and places BOTH together; when first clears but second does not, the port does nothing. Its else arm (:88-95) also runs for q.count===0 where DFU's 'else if (>1)' does nothing. Pins (test/automap_ext.test.js:89-110) do not cover these arms.
consequence: In crowded town automaps the port computes different plate offsets than DFU and can print '*' where DFU shows a name (or vice versa).

title: EXIT click closes bank window while an amount is being typed; DFU's exit is inert then
claim: DFU's ExitButton_OnMouseClick guards with 'if (!transactionInput.Enabled) CloseWindow();' (DaggerfallBankingWindow.cs:476-477) - while a deposit/withdraw/repay amount field is open, EXIT does nothing. The port's click path (bankWindow.js:261) closes unconditionally on the exit rect with no transactionType check (the keyboard path :243-250 does gate Escape to cancel-input-first).
consequence: Clicking EXIT mid-transaction closes the whole bank window instead of being ignored; the typed amount is silently discarded.

title: Guild popup buttons play no ButtonClick sound
claim: DFU plays SoundClips.ButtonClick at the top of every button handler on this window: Talk (:293), Service (:457), Exit (:477), Join (:501). The port's GuildServiceWindow imports no audio; its click()/input() paths (guildServiceWindow.js:151-166, 134-149) fire the hooks silently. Message-box button hits do click (messageBox.js:213), but the four panel buttons never do. The bank windows in the same chunk play the sound, so this is an omission, not a convention.
consequence: Join/Talk/Service/Exit on the guild popup are silent where DFU clicks audibly.

title: Purchase price list uses 7px row pitch; DFU ListBox pitch is glyphHeight+rowSpacing = 8
claim: The port derives LIST_ROW_H = 7 from 'the list is 78 tall, so a row is 7 with the remainder as padding' (bankPurchaseWindow.js:53-56), used for draw (:193) and click mapping (:158). DFU's ListBox never derives row height from list height: Draw advances y += TextHeight + rowSpacing (ListBox.cs:326) and click row = y / (GlyphHeight + rowSpacing) (:434); with default FONT0003 (glyph height 7) and rowSpacing 1 the pitch is 8. The port is internally consistent (draw and hit agree), but rows sit progressively higher than DFU's - 9px drift by row 10.
consequence: House price rows render more tightly packed than DFU/classic; purely visual since the port's hit test uses the same pitch.

title: Room-rental flow closes the tavern window; DFU always returns to the four-button panel
claim: DFU's ROOM button never closes the tavern: :153-171 pushes an input box over it; the box closes ITSELF before OnGotUserInput (DaggerfallInputMessageBox.cs:298-304); invalid input (:176-178) and the 350-day refusal (:188-191) leave the tavern topmost; ConfirmRenting's CloseWindow() (:214) pops the TOP window - the price box pushed at :208 (UserInterfaceWindow.cs:127-132 pops top; DaggerfallMessageBox does not self-close, :479-484). So every room-flow ending returns to the panel. The port runs the chain in a ServiceFlowWindow whose onClose closes the tavern (:140-143); the header :33-35 and test/tavernwindow.test.js:147-160 pin the port while misreading :212's pop-top semantics.
consequence: After renting, declining, a too-many-days refusal, or a typo, the innkeeper panel is gone and the player must re-activate the NPC; in DFU they land back on the four-button panel.

title: Over-limit hours refusal keeps the prompt up; DFU's input box has already closed itself
claim: DFU's TimedRestPrompt_OnGotUserInput runs only after the input box closed itself (DaggerfallInputMessageBox.cs:298-304), so time>99 shows TEXT.RSC 26 over the rest window's SELECTION page; retrying needs a fresh While/Loiter press, which re-runs the gate (:642-657 warning box -> CanRest, with its Vagrancy side effect in town). The port stays in the 'hours' state with the notice above a still-live prompt reset to '0' (restWindow.js:265-270), and a retry re-enters _start without re-running _canRest. restSession.js:235-237 claims 'the prompt STAYS UP' in DFU citing :753-757 - the same misread; those lines show a box and return with no new prompt.
consequence: Different landing page after the 99-hour/loiter-cap refusal, and a retry skips DFU's repeated CanRest gate (e.g. the second Vagrancy registration when camping in town).

title: Tavern buttons play no ButtonClick sound
claim: DFU plays SoundClips.ButtonClick on all four tavern buttons (Exit :135, Room :155, Talk :264, Food :339) and on the food picker's pick (:307). The port's TavernWindow imports no audio module and its click()/input() handlers (tavernWindow.js:235-251) play nothing - unlike sibling native windows (playerHistory.js:83, restWindow.js:238) which do port their ButtonClick one-shots.
consequence: The innkeeper panel is silent where DFU clicks on every button press.

title: Teleport Yes/No play a ButtonClick DFU does not
claim: DaggerfallTeleportPopUp's Yes/No handlers play no sound (No :116-119 just CloseWindow; Yes :153-156 just TeleportAway) and the window never sets Button.ClickSound - Button.ClickHandler plays only when clickSound != null (Button.cs:95-98) and DaggerfallUI.AddButton sets none (DaggerfallUI.cs:981-998). The port's _click() (teleportPopUp.js:87) plays SOUND.ButtonClick in both _yes (:99) and _no (:92).
consequence: An added click sound on the teleport confirmation that DFU does not make.

title: Large HUD branch drops the breath bar DFU keeps enabled
claim: DaggerfallHUD.cs:203 sets breathBar.Enabled = ShowBreathBar every frame, and the large-HUD force-off block (:214-220) disables only vitals, compass and interactionModeIcon - the breath bar stays on and draws while the large HUD is up. The port's drawHud large branch (hud.js:284-293) draws drawHudLarge, the crosshair and the spell rows then returns at line 292, so the breath-bar draw at hud.js:313-323 is unreachable; drawHudLarge (hudLarge.js:324-371) draws no breath bar either. The port's own comment at hud.js:279 ('the CROSSHAIR and the breath bar stay') states the DFU law it then fails to implement; no test pins the omission.
consequence: With GUI/LargeHUD on, a player swimming underwater gets no breath bar at all - no drowning warning until damage starts.

title: EnableVitalsIndicators loss/gain bars unported; default-on DFU behavior missing
claim: HUDVitals.cs adds six indicator bars when EnableVitalsIndicators is true (:99-115): smoothed loss trails (colors :41-46) and gain bars, driven by VitalsChangeDetector events (:290-312) and Cycle() (:282-287); only when false does it take SynchronizeImmediately (:211-214). Port hud.js:300-310 draws only the three plain instant bars - the setting-false path - and nothing in src/ reads GUI/EnableVitalsIndicators (grep: only settingsDefaults.js:106 where it defaults "True", settingsMap.js:162, settingsCopy.js:118, which surface it in the settings screen). Not recorded in hud.js, UI-Arc.md U1, or anywhere else.
consequence: The damage/heal trail DFU shows by default on the HUD bars never appears, and the surfaced 'Vitals Indicators' toggle does nothing.

title: SwapHealthAndFatigueColors setting has no consumer; toggle is inert
claim: HUDVitals.LoadAssets (:181-198) swaps the health and fatigue bar art (MAIN03I0/MAIN04I0) and their indicator colors when Settings.SwapHealthAndFatigueColors is true. The port's loadHud (hud.js:188-190) maps MAIN03I0->health and MAIN04I0->fatigue unconditionally, and no file in src/ reads the key (grep: only settingsDefaults.js:95, settingsCopy.js:137, settingsMap.js:205, which surface it as 'Swap Bar Colours' on the settings screen's Accessibility page). hudLarge.js:349-352 reuses the same unswapped art. Not recorded as a departure anywhere.
consequence: Turning on 'Swap Bar Colours' (DFU's red-health/green-fatigue accessibility swap) changes nothing on either HUD.

title: Book layout merges Text tokens into one row and centers the justify-terminated line, unlike CreateBookLabels
claim: DFU CreateBookLabels creates a SEPARATE label per Text token (:254), each its own row via LayoutBookLabels (y += label.Size.y, :326), with alignment applied only to labels created AFTER a justify token (:241-245). The port (bookReader.js:97-110) concatenates a line's Text tokens into ONE row and applies JustifyCenter retroactively (current.center=true, :103). For Text('A'),0xFD,Text('B'),NewLine (the shape the port's test PAGE1 models), DFU renders 'A' Left and 'B' Center on two rows; the port renders one centered row 'AB'. test/books.test.js:140-153 pins the port (['CenteredOffset line', true]) while citing the C# - the pin restates the port.
consequence: Classic books using 0xFD line terminators (centered title pages, poems) render consecutive centered lines run together on one over-wide row, with centering shifted one line versus DFU.

title: shouldClose drops the unconditional Escape close, making quest and infection videos unskippable
claim: DFU closes the vid window on 'endOnAnyKey && AnyKeyDown || GetBackButtonDown() || EndOfFile && Playing' (:140-142); GetBackButtonDown is Escape keydown (InputManager.cs:1065-1067), checked OUTSIDE the endOnAnyKey gate, so EndOnAnyKey=false videos (PlayVideo.cs:78, VampirismInfection.cs:126/136, LycanthropyInfection.cs:114) still skip on Escape. The port's shouldClose (videoPlayer.js:234-236) is '(endOnAnyKey && anyKeyDown) || (endOfFile && playing)' with no back-button arm, and shared.js:936 passes endOnAnyKey:false for infection videos - its comment even asserts they 'cannot be skipped', misreading DFU.
consequence: The vampirism/lycanthropy dream and turning videos and quest PlayVideo actions cannot be skipped with Escape in the port; in DFU Escape always closes the video window.

title: Settings dialog treats ANY click as the affirmative - drawn Cancel/Keep It buttons confirm on click
claim: click() with a dialog open (settingsWindow.js:469-475) runs 'this.dialog = null; if (d.onYes) d.onYes(); else if (d.buttons?.[0]?.id === 'yes') this._commit(d.key, 'False')' with NO hit-test of the dialog's buttons, while _drawDialog (:639-646) renders distinct buttons including refusals ('Cancel' on Reset Everything :460, 'Keep It' on the ShowOptionsAtStart lock-out :302). Only the keyboard path (:419-431) treats Escape as refusal. So a pointer click on the drawn Cancel button - or anywhere - executes onYes (resetToDefaults :461) or commits 'False'. test/settingsUI.test.js:308-312 pins click-anywhere-runs-the-action, restating the port.
consequence: A mouse/touch player tapping 'Cancel' on Reset Everything wipes every settings override; tapping 'Keep It' disables the settings-at-start option anyway. No pointer path can decline a dialog.

title: Quest-item transfer guard missing; playerDropped never written, DroppedItemAtPlace can never fire
claim: DFU TransferItem (DaggerfallInventoryWindow.cs:1480-1505) refuses moving a quest item out of the pack when CanDropQuestItems is false (default False in both; port settingsDefaults.js:124) unless questItem.AllowDrop, and on a legal drop sets PlayerDropped=true (:1497-1498), clearing it on pickup (:1499-1500). The port's Remove arm (nativeInventory.js:453-501) and remote pickup (:549-594) guard only Transportation (:464) and summoned (:472). The port's quest Item has playerDropped (quest/item.js:78) and DroppedItemAtPlace reads it (actions.js:1871) - but nothing in src/ ever sets playerDropped=true; its only DFU writer is this missing arm.
consequence: Players can drop/wagon-stash undroppable quest items, and every 'dropped item at place' quest objective is permanently uncompletable - the trigger polls a flag no code path can set.

title: Remote-list quest item click never fires setPlayerClicked
claim: DFU RemoteItemListScroller_OnItemClick's first act (DaggerfallInventoryWindow.cs:2027-2037): if item.IsQuestItem, resolve the quest Item and call SetPlayerClicked() - before any action-mode branch. The port's _pickRemote (nativeInventory.js:549-594) has no such call; setPlayerClicked fires only from world-flat clicks and NPC sweeps (resourceBehaviour.js:148, machine.js:510), never from the inventory window. The ClickedItem trigger consumes item.hasPlayerClicked (systems/quest/actions.js:484).
consequence: A quest item riding a foe (corpse loot) or any loot container: taking it through the loot window adds it to the bag but the 'clicked item' task never triggers - the quest stalls.

title: Sell staging bypasses every TransferItem guard: summoned, quest, loaded-cart, map
claim: DFU's Sell/SellMagic local click routes through TransferItem (DaggerfallTradeWindow.cs:795), inheriting its guards: summoned refused with 'cannotRemoveItem' (DaggerfallInventoryWindow.cs:1464-1469), quest items refused (:1481-1494), maps consumed via RecordLocationFromMap (:1471-1478); the trade window also blocks selling the cart while the wagon holds items (DaggerfallTradeWindow.cs:789-793). The port's _pickLocal (nativeTrade.js:187-199) calls localClickDecision (tradeModes.js:350-371) which answers {kind:'stage'} unconditionally for Sell/SellMagic, and _move (:150-154) is a raw splice/push with no guard.
consequence: Players can sell summoned (soon-to-vanish) items and quest-critical items to shops, and sell the cart out from under a loaded wagon - all refused or special-cased in DFU.

title: TransferItem's map arm missing: maps transfer as items instead of revealing a location
claim: DFU TransferItem's first content arm (DaggerfallInventoryWindow.cs:1471-1478): a MiscItems.Map item transferred in either direction (remove-drop or loot pickup) calls RecordLocationFromMap and removes it - it never lands in the destination. The port implements the reveal only in the Use-mode arm (useItem.js:220-236 via revealMap); _pick's Remove arm (nativeInventory.js:464-501) and _pickRemote (:549-594) transfer a map like any other item.
consequence: Picking a treasure map out of a loot pile (the common classic route) puts the map in the bag instead of revealing a location and consuming it; dropping one stashes it instead of revealing.

title: Lit light source not extinguished when transferred out of the pack
claim: DFU TransferItem (DaggerfallInventoryWindow.cs:1506-1508): 'if (item.IsLightSource && playerEntity.LightSource == item && from == localItems) playerEntity.LightSource = null'. The port tracks entity.lightSource (playerTorch.js:113-135, useItem.js:263-267) but the inventory Remove transfer (nativeInventory.js:482-501) and the trade sell staging (nativeTrade.js:195) never clear it.
consequence: Dropping or selling a lit torch/lantern leaves entity.lightSource pointing at an item no longer carried - the player keeps the light (and its condition burn) from an item lying in a pile or a shop.

title: Buy-mode basket staging skips the CanCarryAmount gate
claim: DFU's Buy remote click transfers shelf->basket through TransferItem with maxAmount=CanCarryAmount(item) (DaggerfallTradeWindow.cs:842): zero capacity shows 'cannotCarryAnymore' and refuses (DaggerfallInventoryWindow.cs:1414-1422), a partial fit splits. The port's _pickRemote (nativeTrade.js:204-209) moves the whole item into the basket with no capacity check.
consequence: A player can stage and buy arbitrarily heavy lots that DFU would refuse or split at basket time, ending up over MaxEncumbrance through the shop screen.

title: Conversation scroll arrows missing; history pinned to newest and unreadable
claim: DFU's talk window has conversation up/down arrows at (303,64,9,16)/(303,176,9,16) (DaggerfallTalkWindow.cs:226-227, wired :798-804) whose handlers move the conversation scrollbar +/-5px (:1442-1452), plus the scrollbar at (305,81). The port's TALK_RECTS (nativeTalk.js:40-57) has no conversation arrows, and draw() recomputes scroll as max(0, contentH - panelH) every frame (:106, :338), permanently pinning the panel to the last row.
consequence: Once the conversation exceeds 126px the player cannot scroll back to re-read earlier answers (directions, names) that DFU keeps reachable.

title: Journal log-entry clicks are inert: no travel-map jump, no move/remove/add-note
claim: DFU's questLogLabel takes clicks and right-clicks (DaggerfallQuestJournalWindow.cs:153-154) into HandleClick (:385-436): on Active Quests a click offers a travel-map jump to the quest's place (FindPlace_OnButtonClick :353-363); on notebook/finished pages click offers move, right-click remove, a click between entries adds a note, and the title-panel click opens EnterNote (:297-300). The port's click() (questJournal.js:182-191) consumes the log and title rects as no-ops and no other member implements these flows.
consequence: Players cannot jump to a quest location from the journal, nor add, move, or remove notebook/finished-quest entries - all standard DFU journal interactions.

title: F6 near a dungeon exit opens wagon in Remove mode; DFU keeps Equip
claim: DFU CheckWagonAccess's proximity branch (DaggerfallInventoryWindow.cs:1089-1096) only sets allowDungeonWagonAccess and ShowWagon(true) - the action mode stays the Equip default from OnPush (:649-653). SelectActionMode(Remove) happens only in the first branch (:1084-1088), reached via the exit-door prompt's AllowDungeonWagonAccess (PlayerActivate.cs:1141). The port's constructor (nativeInventory.js:218-219) merges both flows: a near-exit open sets usingWagon AND mode='remove'.
consequence: Opening inventory near a dungeon exit with a cart, a local-list click transfers the item into the wagon instead of equipping it - the opposite default of DFU's plain F6 flow.

title: chooseOne: DFU blocks all local Remove transfers; port allows staging into the wagon
claim: DFU's local Remove arm runs only 'if (remoteItems != null && !chooseOne)' (DaggerfallInventoryWindow.cs:1994) - while a choose-one reward list is up nothing leaves the pack regardless of wagon state. The port's guard (nativeInventory.js:474) is 'if (this.chooseOne && !this.usingWagon) return', and _wagon (:381-393) has no chooseOne gate, so a cart owner can toggle the wagon and transfer pack items into it mid-choose-one.
consequence: During a guild reward choose-one window, a cart owner can move pack items into the wagon where DFU makes the local list inert.

title: Journal highlight tokens draw orange; DFU overrides HighlightColor to white here
claim: The port's JOURNAL_COLORS.highlight is (219,130,40), citing DaggerfallHighlightTextColor as the MultiFormatTextLabel default (questJournal.js:69-80). But DaggerfallQuestJournalWindow.cs:152 explicitly sets 'questLogLabel.HighlightColor = Color.white', so TextHighlight tokens (date/city and finished-quest headers) render white in this window (MultiFormatTextLabel.cs:362-364 uses HighlightColor).
consequence: Every notebook date header and finished-quest header shows orange where DFU shows white.

title: Character sheet stat labels lack drained/increased colors
claim: DFU UpdatePlayerValues (DaggerfallCharacterSheetWindow.cs:414-419) colors each stat label DaggerfallUnityStatDrainedTextColor (190,85,24) when live < permanent and DaggerfallUnityStatIncreasedTextColor (178,207,255) when live > permanent (DaggerfallUI.cs:65-66). The port draws all eight stats via label() with the shadowText default color (charsheet.js:289-290; nativePanel.js:24, :87).
consequence: A player with drained (disease/spell) or fortified stats sees them in the normal yellow - the at-a-glance drain warning DFU gives is absent.

title: Conversation questions left-aligned; DFU right-aligns question rows
claim: DFU SetQuestionAnswerPairInConversationListbox sets the question label's HorizontalAlignment to Right (DaggerfallTalkWindow.cs:1259) while answers are Left (:1270). The port draws every conversation line at the panel's left edge R.conversation[0] (nativeTalk.js:344-345) regardless of kind.
consequence: The classic visual distinction (player questions hugging the right margin, NPC answers the left) is lost in the conversation log.

title: Forced (child) enchantment rows can be removed by clicking them
claim: DFU's EnchantmentPanel_OnMouseClick only removes a panel when panel.Enchantment.ParentEnchantment == 0 ('child panels are removed by clicking on parent', EnchantmentListPicker.cs:268-271). The port's click handler (itemMakerWindow.js:338-344) hit-tests any visible row and calls _removeRow(hit.entry) with no parentEnchantment guard; removeEnchantment (enchantmentCatalogue.js:360-362) then filters the clicked entry out by its own key, so a forced child (which carries parentEnchantment = parent key and its own key) is removed on its own. The catalogue's comment even codifies 'a child removed on its own takes nothing', which contradicts DFU where a child cannot be removed at all.
consequence: A player soul-binding a Daedra Lord can click away the forced Extra Weight / User Takes Damage side effects and keep the soul-bound power without its drawbacks, which DFU forbids.

title: Enchanting a stacked item enchants the whole stack (no SplitStack)
claim: DFU's EnchantButton_OnMouseClick splits one item off a stack before enchanting: 'if (selectedItem.IsAStack()) selectedItem = ...Items.SplitStack(selectedItem, 1)' (cs:752-754). The port's _enchant (itemMakerWindow.js:277-294) calls applyEnchantments(this.selected, ...) directly, and applyEnchantments (enchanting.js:200-206) just sets item.enchantments on the object - no stack split anywhere. Gems (Ingredients tab, itemMakerFilter line 120) are stackable in the port (inventory.js isStackable:110 - ingredients stack), so a merged stack of N gems is a single selectable item.
consequence: Enchanting a stack of e.g. 5 rubies produces 5 enchanted rubies for one gold payment and one enchantment-point budget; DFU enchants exactly one split-off gem.

title: Item maker gold check and label use coins only, excluding letters of credit
claim: DFU's item maker reads PlayerEntity.GetGoldAmount() for the available-gold label (DaggerfallItemMakerWindow.cs:193) and the enchant affordability check (cs:734-739); GetGoldAmount returns goldPieces + items.GetCreditAmount() (PlayerEntity.cs:1313-1316). The port's gold() (itemMakerWindow.js:189) calls goldAmount(), the coin purse alone (court.js:151-152); enchantDecision's gold test (enchanting.js:188) and the label both ride it. The port's own comment at :282-284 says the deduction seam spends letters of credit - but the gating check never counts them.
consequence: A player whose wealth sits in letters of credit is refused ('You do not have the gold to properly pay the enchanter') where DFU lets the enchant proceed, and the shown gold figure is understated.

title: Cast When Used/Held/Strikes list rows print the wrong spell name
claim: DFU's EnchantmentPanel prints enchantment.SecondaryDisplayName - the actual spell name stored in the settings (EnchantmentListPicker.cs:333-334). The port draws the secondary row as names[row.entry.param] (itemMakerWindow.js:390-393), where names = enchantmentParams(type) is a DENSE list-ordered array (enchantmentCatalogue.js:193-201) but entry.param for the three CastWhen* effects is the sparse classic SPELL ID (catalogue :171, stored at :233). E.g. CastWhenUsed param 12 is Resist Fire, but names[12] is 'Fireball'; param 94 (Recall) indexes past the array and prints blank. The picker itself is correct (labels[i] aligned by index, catalogue :493-495) - only the list rows mis-index.
consequence: After picking 'Cast when used - Resist Fire' the powers list shows 'Fireball' (or a blank) under Cast When Used; nearly every CastWhen* row names the wrong spell.

title: Enchantment lists cannot scroll; overflowing rows are invisible and unremovable
claim: DFU's EnchantmentListPicker shows a slim scrollbar when enchantmentPanels.Count > 7 (ShowScroller, cs:244-247), narrows rows to 71 wide, and scrolls via wheel (MouseScrollUp/Down cs:180-196) and the scroller. The port's draw loop breaks at 'if (row.y + row.h > rect[3]) break' (itemMakerWindow.js:385), computes 'scrolled' and voids it (:383, :395), and neither click() (:338-344) nor input() offers any scroll path for the two lists. With rows carrying secondary names (12px + 5 gap), only 7 rows fit in the 120px rect, so an 8th+ row (reachable: up to 10 enchantments, e.g. eight Cast When Used spells) is off-panel.
consequence: Enchantments past the seventh two-line row can be neither seen nor clicked off; DFU scrolls to them.

title: Item rename caps at 26 characters vs DFU's TextBox default 31
claim: DFU's rename runs through DaggerfallInputMessageBox whose TextBox default maxCharacters is 31 (TextBox.cs:26), and RenameItem itself imposes no cap (DaggerfallUnityItem.cs:1348-1354). The port's inline rename field (a recorded widget departure) stops accepting characters at 26 (itemMakerWindow.js:316: 'this.itemName.length < 26').
consequence: Item names 27-31 characters long, legal in DFU, cannot be typed in the port's rename strip.

title: Recipe pick partially fills the cauldron instead of refusing when ingredients are missing
claim: DFU's AddRecipeToCauldron: if any recipe ingredient is unmatched it shows GetLocalizedText("reqIngredients") and adds NOTHING (cs:297-301); otherwise it ClearCauldron()s first, adds every ingredient, and sets nameLabel = recipeName (cs:302-308). The port's _fillFrom (potionMakerWindow.js:184-194) adds whatever gatherRecipe found (potions.js:229-239) - no missing-ingredient message, no cauldron clear (fills on top of existing contents), no name label. potions.js:224-228's comment claims DFU 'fills what it can... does not refuse', which the C# contradicts; potionmakerwindow.test.js:180-191 pins the port behavior while citing :283-309 - the pin restates the port.
consequence: Picking a recipe while missing one herb silently loads an incomplete cauldron; mixing burns the ingredients on a useless potion, where DFU refuses with a message. Picking with leftovers in the pot also mixes them in.

title: Mixing an empty cauldron shows the failure message instead of doing nothing
claim: DFU's MixButton_OnMouseClick plays the click and only calls MixCauldron() 'if (cauldron.Count > 0)' (cs:396-397). The port's _mix (potionMakerWindow.js:151-169) has no emptiness guard: mixCauldron([]) hashes the empty list, matches no recipe, and the window shows the POTION_FAILED box ('The ingredients you have combined are useless.').
consequence: Clicking MIX (or pressing M/Enter) with an empty pot pops a failure message box that DFU never shows.

title: Enchanted ingredients are not excluded from the potion maker's list
claim: DFU's Refresh collects ingredients with 'if (item.IsIngredient && !item.IsEnchanted)' (cs:148), and the consume walk also passes allowEnchantedItem: false (cs:338, :345). The port's ingredients() (potionMakerWindow.js:125-133) filters with isIngredient(it) alone (potions.js:184 - template flag only), so an enchanted gem (mintable at the port's own item maker, which lists Gems) appears in the ingredient grid and can be added to the cauldron and consumed.
consequence: A player can grind an enchanted ruby into a potion - and the takeOne consumption may instead burn an unenchanted one - where DFU keeps enchanted items out of the pot entirely.

title: Ingredient list never scrolls: this.scroll has no writer
claim: DFU's ingredientsListScroller is a scrolling ItemListScroller (4 rows x 3 cols, cs:226-233) with scroll handling for an arbitrary ingredient count. The port initializes this.scroll = 0 (potionMakerWindow.js:113) and reads it at :216 and :234, but nothing in click() or input() ever modifies it - grep confirms those are the only three references. Only the first 12 ingredient stacks are ever shown or clickable.
consequence: A player holding more than 12 distinct ingredient stacks (routine for an alchemist) can never see or use ingredients 13+, and recipes needing them can only be loaded via the RECIPES button.

title: Adding an ingredient from a stack hides the whole stack (no SplitStack)
claim: DFU's AddToCauldron splits one unit off a stack before moving it: 'if (item.IsAStack()) item = ingredients.SplitStack(item, 1)' (cs:256-257), leaving the remainder visible and addable. The port's _addToCauldron (potionMakerWindow.js:137-141) pushes the stack OBJECT into the cauldron, and ingredients() (:125-133) removes it from the list by identity, so a stack of N elderberries vanishes entirely from the grid while one conceptual unit is in the pot; a second unit of the same stack cannot be added.
consequence: With merged ingredient stacks (the port stacks ingredients per inventory.js:110), the remaining N-1 units are invisible and unusable while one is in the cauldron; DFU shows and offers the remainder.

title: Name label is set on successful mix; DFU sets it only on recipe fill
claim: DFU's MixCauldron never touches nameLabel (cs:311-360); the label is written only by AddRecipeToCauldron ('nameLabel.Text = recipeName', cs:307) and cleared by every add/remove. The port inverts this: _mix sets this.nameLabel = result.recipe.name on success (potionMakerWindow.js:158) while _fillFrom leaves it blank (finding on :184 above). potionmakerwindow.test.js:136 pins the port's mix-time label.
consequence: The bottom-left name label shows the potion name after mixing (it stays blank in DFU) and stays blank after a recipe fill (where DFU shows the recipe name).

title: Potion maker gold label wired to coins only, not GetGoldAmount
claim: DFU's potion maker label reads GameManager.Instance.PlayerEntity.GetGoldAmount() (cs:138), which is goldPieces + letters of credit (PlayerEntity.cs:1313-1316). The host hands the window 'gold: () => goldAmount(playerEntity)' (worldModes.js:1741) - the coin purse only (court.js:151-152) - which potionMakerWindow.js:246 prints.
consequence: The gold figure in the potion maker understates a player's wealth when part of it is letters of credit (display only - no purchase rides it).

title: Sort-by-cost applies the lycanthropy free-cast quirk; DFU sorts by real cost
claim: DFU's SortSpellsPointCost orders by the raw CalculateTotalEffectCosts spell-point cost (DaggerfallEntity.cs:743-748) with no tag check - the lycanthropy 0-display quirk lives only in PopulateSpellsList (DaggerfallSpellBookWindow.cs:264-267). The port's confirmSort cost map uses spellPointCost(sp, castCost) (spellbookWindow.js:511), which returns 0 for the lycanthropy tag (:212-215), so that spell sorts to the front instead of to its true-cost position.
consequence: For a lycanthrope, the second (cost) sort pass places the lycanthropy spell first in the book rather than where its real casting cost puts it in DFU.

title: Spellbook scroll bar is drawn but not interactive
claim: DFU's VerticalScrollBar supports thumb dragging (Update, cs:104-128) and click-above/below-thumb paging by displayUnits (MouseClick, cs:140-148), wired to the list via OnScroll (DaggerfallSpellBookWindow.cs:371, :794-797). The port draws the thumb (spellbookWindow.js:784-789) but click() (:649-705) has no branch for SPELLBOOK_RECTS.scrollBar - a click there falls through to 'return true' with no effect, and there is no drag path.
consequence: With more than 16 spells, clicking or dragging the scroll bar does nothing; only the wheel and arrow buttons scroll, where DFU also pages and drags.

title: Spell maker ignores allowedTargets/allowedElements restrictions from chosen effects
claim: DFU restricts target and element to what the chosen effects allow: SetSpellTarget returns early when '(allowedTargets & targetType) == TargetTypes.None' (cs:499-501), SetSpellElement likewise (cs:527-530), and UpdateAllowedButtons recomputes allowedTargets as the INTERSECTION of each effect's Properties.AllowedTargets and allowedElements as magic-only union (cs:563-601), forcing the selection back to the first allowed value. The port's _inputMain cycles rangeType and element freely through all five values (spellMakerWindow.js:187-190) and no allowedTargets/allowedElements state exists anywhere in src/ (grep confirms).
consequence: The port will price and inscribe combinations DFU forbids - e.g. an 'Area at Range' spell from a caster-only effect - producing spells with wrong target semantics and costs that classic/DFU can never mint.

title: envAttack skips Receive(Attack) on doors; DFU fires the door's action record before bashing
claim: DFU WeaponEnvDamage (WeaponManager.cs:460-464) calls action.Receive(player, Attack) on ANY hit object with a DaggerfallAction - including an action door (one GameObject, both components) - and THEN (:467-471) calls actionDoor.AttemptBash(true). Port envAttack (weaponRig.js:159-162): a door branch does attemptBash and returns; only non-doors get receive('Attack'). So an Attack/MultiTrigger-flagged door record (Castle Wayrest doors are MultiTrigger, DaggerfallActionDoor.cs:263 comment) never fires on a weapon hit; the bash path's _execOwnAction passes only the 'Door' trigger, which those flags reject. test/weaponrig.test.js:83 pins the port's behavior, restating the port.
consequence: Attacking an Attack/MultiTrigger action door (e.g. Castle Wayrest DoorText doors whose record runs the trespass check) never fires its record in the port; DFU fires it on every weapon hit.

title: Dungeon castle/special-area ambient (0.58) unported - castle blocks render at 0.12
claim: PlayerAmbientLight.UpdateAmbientLight (:84-92) selects CastleAmbientLight (0.58) inside dungeon castle blocks, SpecialAreaLight (0.58) in special areas, DungeonAmbientLight (0.12) otherwise. The port exports only DUNGEON_AMBIENT [0.12,0.12,0.12] (dungeonLights.js:14) and both dungeon hosts apply it unconditionally (worldModes.js:2747, dungeon.js:247). The castle predicate exists live in the port (dungeonContext.js:2012 castleBlockAt, used for music and water sounds, exposed at :2524) but is never consulted for ambient - a law input computed and thrown away at the seam.
consequence: Non-hostile castle wings (Castle Daggerfall/Wayrest/Sentinel) render at ambient 0.12 instead of 0.58 - about 5x darker than DFU; the brighten-in-castle-block behavior is absent.

title: Door close sound fires at swing start; DFU plays it when the close completes
claim: DFU Close() (:311-332) starts the reverse tween and plays NO sound; CloseSound plays in OnCompleteClose (:339-346), after the 1.5 s swing, just before the collider re-solidifies. The port's _closeDoor (actionSystem.js:656-657) emits onDoorState(o, false) at close START and both hosts play the clip immediately (dungeonContext.js:199-202, interiorContext.js:51-54). Open-side timing matches DFU (sound at open start, :296-302 vs actionSystem.js:645).
consequence: Every door close is audible ~1.5 s early - the shut sound plays while the door is still swinging instead of when it lands closed as in DFU.

title: Port persists activationCount across save/load; DFU resets it to 0
claim: SerializableActionObject (:55-88) persists only position/rotation/currentState/tween percentage; SerializableActionDoor (:67-101) adds lock and FailedSkillLevel. Neither serializes DaggerfallAction.activationCount, and the scene rebuilds on load, so every counter restarts at 0 in DFU. The port saves it for every object (actionSystem.js:830-832) and restores it (:858-859). Save-relevant state semantics are in the byte-exact doctrine list.
consequence: After loading, DFU re-shows a DoorText door's text and holds it shut on first click, and restarts Hurt21's every-20th phase; the port does neither, so trap cadence and first-click door behavior diverge after any save/load.

title: LightningPlayer slots are always 2 frames; DFU's skipped flash is a 1-frame slot
claim: DFU PlayLightningEffects (:367-382): per flash, `if (Random.value < 0.6) { on; yield; }` then unconditionally off + yield - a skipped flash consumes ONE frame, a lit one two. The port (weather.js:169-179) always spends two frames per slot, and its comment claims parity with 'the coroutine's WaitForEndOfFrame pairs'. Also DFU re-arms the next 4-35 s wait at strike time (:146-152), while the port re-arms after the sequence ends (:176-179).
consequence: Storm flash sequences run up to ~2x the frames of DFU (a 20-30 flash roll is ~0.3-0.5 s longer at 60 fps) and successive strikes drift slightly later; visual timing only.

title: failedSkillLevel omitted from save snapshot (in-code FLAGGED gap, confirmed)
claim: SerializableActionDoor saves lockpickFailedSkillLevel (:77) and restores it (:99-101), so DFU's lockpick retry gate (FailedSkillLevel == live skill, DaggerfallActionDoor.cs:157) survives save/load. The port's collectSaveData (actionSystem.js:829-837) omits failedSkillLevel and restore never sets it, resetting it to 0 on load. The port already flags this at addDoor (:460-467, 'FLAGGED, a live gap'). Reported to confirm the flag is accurate - both sides read this session.
consequence: A player who failed a pick at their current skill can save+load and immediately retry the same lock; DFU blocks the retry until the live skill changes.

title: Nature scatter rect exclusion gated on pre-expansion mins; DFU re-checks the expanded rect per tile
claim: DFU LayoutNature expands the location rect by natureClearance=4 only when the un-expanded rect has x>0 && y>0 (TerrainNature.cs:60-66), then in the tile loop re-evaluates `rect.x > 0 && rect.y > 0 && rect.Contains(tilePos)` on the EXPANDED rect (TerrainNature.cs:124) - so when expansion pushes xMin or yMin to <= 0, DFU disables the containment test entirely and scatters nature inside the location footprint. The port (terrainNature.js:72-79) builds the rect when the PRE-expansion mins are > 0 and then applies containment unconditionally at line 112, never re-checking the expanded mins.
consequence: For a location whose pre-clearance rect min on either axis lies in (0, 4] (only possible for 8-block-wide/tall locations, since the tile origin is 0 only then), DFU places nature billboards over the town footprint while the port suppresses them - a visible foliage difference at large walled cities with narrow edge blend space.

title: Quest item use never sets useClicked - ItemUsedDo quests cannot advance
