claim: DFU UseItem sets questItem.UseClicked=true on a use click and shows the item's UsedMessageID popup (InventoryWindow.cs:1681-1700); the port's ItemUsedDo action is live and polls item.useClicked (systems/quest/actions.js:1028-1038), but no site in src/ ever sets useClicked=true - quest/item.js:74 initializes it false, useItem() only attaches a 'questItem:true' rider (useItem.js:190-195), and nativeInventory._useResult ignores that rider. isParchment/isClothing (useItem.js:77-79), ported verbatim for exactly this DFU block's parchment/clothing exception, have zero callers.
consequence: Any quest using '<item> used do <task>' or 'used saying' stalls forever - using the quest item does nothing, the task never starts, and quest letters' used-message popup never shows.

title: Exterior static NPCs are inert - collectExteriorNpcs has no caller
claim: DFU RMBLayout adds a StaticNPC behaviour plus QuestMachine.SetupIndividualStaticNPC to every exterior RMB flat with FactionID != 0 (RMBLayout.cs:370-377 and :446-453), making them clickable talk/quest targets. The port translated the filter (collectExteriorNpcs, exteriorNpcs.js:12-14) but no host calls it: world.js:455-457 and exterior.js:312 add all block flats as plain billboards via addFlat, and the only static-NPC talk paths (worldModes.js:978/1365 talkToStaticNPC) come from collectInteriorPeople.
consequence: NPC flats standing outdoors - courtyard nobles, guards, and individual quest NPCs placed in town exteriors - can never be clicked or talked to, and individual-NPC quest hooks outside never fire.

title: Alliance/war/ruler mutators ported but the 38-day conditions update never calls them
claim: DFU PlayerEntity.RegionPowerAndConditionsUpdate(true) wires GetNumberOfCommonAlliesAndEnemies (:1698/:1718/:1760), StartFactionAllies (:1766), StartFactionEnemies (:1904) and SetNewRulerData (:1931) into the 38-day tick. The port carries faithful translations (factionRelations.js:109/221/247/299/309, regionConditions.resetWarDataForRegion:162) with zero callers: worldTick.js:507-510's 38-day arm calls only regionPowerUpdate, and its comment flags the conditions body while stale-claiming the mutators are 'unported' - they exist one module away.
consequence: Regional wars never start or end, alliances never shift, rulers never change, and region condition flags (war/plague etc.) never flip - talk news, war rumors, and condition-driven shop/quest state stay frozen for the whole game.

title: Travel map hasShip hardwired false - ship ownership and knight free-ship perk unwired
claim: DFU computes hasShip = DaggerfallBankManager.OwnsShip || GuildManager.FreeShipTravel() (TravelPopUp.cs:219). The port ships both halves - banking.ownsShip is live in worldModes.js:1231 and KnightlyOrder rank-6 freeShipTravel is ported (guildServices.js:336, zero callers) - but buildTravelMapWindow passes the literal `hasShip: false` (world.js:1728, with a stale 'a SHIP still has no ownership state' comment) and neither call site (world.js:1692/:1702) overrides it, so calculateTripCost's !hasShip arm (travel.js:86) always charges.
consequence: A player who bought a ship, or reached rank 6 in a knightly order, still pays 25 gold per 24 ocean pixels on every fast travel crossing water.

title: IncreasedWeightAllowance enchantment computed but never reaches encumbrance
claim: DFU GetMaxEncumbrance adds amount * IncreasedWeightAllowanceMultiplier on top of FormulaHelper.MaxEncumbrance (DaggerfallEntity.cs:500-508). The port folds the enchantment into _enchantMods.weightAllowanceMult (enchantments.js:390-392, +25%/+50% Held constant) and exposes enchantWeightAllowanceMult (:734) - which has zero callers; every maxEncumbrance consumer (nativeInventory.js:544, charsheet.js:288, worldModes.js:724/:1294, chargen.js:400) passes raw strength*1.5 only (formulas.js:46).
consequence: Items enchanted with Increased Weight Allowance never raise carry capacity - the enchantment is a no-op for encumbrance display, inventory refusals, and every weight gate.

title: Failed witches-coven summoning spawns no daedra - DAEDRIC_FOES table orphaned
claim: DFU spawns CreateFoeSpawner(true, daedricFoes[Random.Range(0,5)], Random.Range(1,4), 4, 64) when a summoning fails at a witches coven (QuestPopupWindow.cs:255-257). The port ports the five-foe table (daedraSummoning.js:80-82, zero callers) and attemptSummoning returns spawnFoes:true (:166), but the host's failure arm (worldModes.js:1663-1669) only console.warns - its own comment FLAGS that the interior has no foe pool - and shows the failure text.
consequence: Failing a coven summoning is consequence-free: the 1-3 daedra that should attack the player never appear.

title: Journal click-to-find-place dead - getMessageResources has no caller
claim: DFU's quest journal handles a click on an active quest entry (JournalWindow.cs:401 -> HandleQuestClicks :439-466) by calling GetMessageResources (:471-485) to find the last Place mentioned, then offers 'Find <location> in <region>?' and sends the travel map there (GotoPlace :360). The port translated getMessageResources (questMacros.js:549-565, zero callers), and questJournal.click (ui/questJournal.js:182-191) merely consumes clicks inside the log rect without inspecting the entry.
consequence: Players cannot click a journal quest entry to locate its destination on the travel map - a core classic navigation aid is missing.

title: expandLetterSignoff never called - every quest letter reads as bare Parchment
claim: DFU ResolveItemLongName returns 'Letter: <signoff line>' for quest parchment by calling QuestMacroHelper.ExpandLetterSignoff (ItemHelper.cs:335-348). The port carries a documented verbatim translation (questMacros.js:492-537 incl. the one-line bug-for-bug walk and 'Letter: ' prefix) with zero callers: item labels come from worldModes._itemLabel (:633, plain name??template name), and quest/item.js:89-93's own comment concedes the long-name maker is not built.
consequence: Quest letters all display as 'Parchment' in the inventory - with two letters from two quests there is no way to tell them apart without using each one.

title: Vampire/mortal dual membership book ported but hosts use a plain object
claim: DFU GuildManager keeps separate membership dictionaries and swaps them by HasVampirism() (GuildManager.cs:107-111, vampMemberships). The port translated the dual-book store - newMembershipStore/membershipsFor(store, hasVampirism)/clearMembershipData (guilds.js:444-459), zero callers - while every host reads `playerEntity.guildMemberships ??= {}` directly (worldModes.js:1319/:1379/:3046/:3062), one book regardless of vampirism, even though the vampirism infection arc is live (infection.js V1).
consequence: A player turned vampire keeps all mortal guild ranks and services (and vice versa on cure) instead of DFU's separate vampire ledger.

title: Disease contracted message (TEXT.RSC 100+type) has no consumer - Status action is dead
claim: DFU's health status box shows each active disease's ContractedMessageTokens (DaggerfallUI.cs:1662-1666; DiseaseEffect.GetClassicContractedMessageTokens :201 reads record 100+diseaseType). The port carries contractedMessageRecord (diseases.js:90, zero callers, its own comment says 'that UI pends'), and the Status input action requires ctx.showStatus (ui/input.js:162) which no host anywhere in src/ provides.
consequence: After incubation a player has no way to learn WHICH disease they carry - only the generic daily 'You feel somewhat bad.' - so choosing the right temple cure or gauging urgency is guesswork.

title: canAccessLibrary ported but library bookshelves are absent entirely
claim: DFU gates guild library bookshelves on guild.CanAccessLibrary() (DaggerfallBookshelf.cs:74; Temple.cs:466, MagesGuild.cs:129 rank>=2). The port translated the gate faithfully (guildServices.js:286-290, zero callers) but the consumer never got built: worldModes.js:638 returns for any non-shop building with the comment 'Library/Guild/Temple bookshelves ... pend (FLAGGED)'.
consequence: Mages Guild and temple libraries are unreadable at any rank - the rank-2 library privilege the port already computes buys nothing.

title: Filled soul traps never show their soul in item lists - soulTrapNameSuffix orphaned
claim: DFU appends ' (<soul name>)' to a filled soul trap's long name (ItemHelper.cs:352-363). The port translated the tail verbatim (soulTrapNameSuffix, mysticism.js:379-385) with zero callers - inventory/shop labels use plain item names (worldModes._itemLabel:633). Only the item info panel's %hs macro (itemInfo.js:191) reveals the soul.
consequence: A player with several soul traps cannot tell filled from empty or which soul is which from any item list; only opening Info on each trap reveals it.

title: Make Potions opens with zero ingredients instead of the record-34 refusal
claim: DFU MakePotionService scans pack+wagon for any ingredient and pops MessageBox(NoPotionIngredients) when none exist (GuildServicePopupWindow.cs:670-686). The port ports the id (NO_POTION_INGREDIENTS=34, guildServiceFlow.js:31, zero callers) but worldModes.js:1736-1758 opens the PotionMakerWindow unconditionally.
consequence: With no ingredients the player gets an empty mixer window instead of the classic 'You have no ingredients' refusal - cosmetic flow divergence only.

title: Duplicate hudCtx toggleRest key: complete outdoor rest path dead, crippled twin runs
claim: hudCtx defines toggleRest twice (:1922 outdoorRestDeps path, :1932 toggleExteriorRest); the later wins, so the full S40 path (outdoorRestDeps :1377: areEnemiesNearby({resting:true}), tickQuests, endLines) is dead code. The live exteriorRestDeps (:960): (a) enemiesNearby = activeCount()>0, but GameManager.cs:684-702 skips a foe that cannot see you beyond 12 units - any live guard anywhere refuses rest (TEXT 354); (b) no tickQuests - a rested night runs zero quest ticks (DaggerfallRestWindow.cs:376-379); (c) TEXT.RSC reader keyed textLines (:963), not the endLines createRestDeps composes (shared.js:1177). Pins restwhere:170 / restlodging:589 each match one arm and miss the shadowing.
consequence: Outdoors: rest refused while any guard lives; quest clocks frozen through rested nights; no wake/healed box at rest end (EndRest 353/350, DaggerfallRestWindow.cs:449-505); the >99-hours refusal (TEXT 26) is silent.

title: Same duplicate toggleRest key in ?exterior: rest blocks on any guard, loses end text
claim: exterior.js:1016 toggleRest (outdoorRestDeps :636, areEnemiesNearby(cityGuards.guards,{resting:true}) + endLines) is shadowed by :1027 toggleExteriorRest, so every Rest key/panel runs exteriorRestDeps (:928): enemiesNearby is activeCount()>0 - exactly what the dead deps' comment (:643-647) warns 'would block sleep for good the moment one guard spawned anywhere in town' - and the TEXT.RSC reader is keyed textLines (:931), not endLines, so RestWindow._end gets null and closes silently. DFU gates rest open via AreEnemiesNearby(true) (DaggerfallUI.cs:652) and hourly via the same resting variant (DaggerfallRestWindow.cs:403): an unaware enemy blocks only within 12 units.
consequence: On the ?town page, one spawned guard anywhere refuses rest (re-arming the enemy alert on every press) until the crime clears; a completed rest shows no wake/healed message box.

title: Dungeon hosts never run the 8-hour enemy-alert decay
claim: decayEnemyAlert's only caller in src/ is shared.createPlayerTicker.tick (shared.js:746), and neither dungeon host builds a ticker: dungeonContext's frame body calls tickPlayerMinutes directly (:2100) and its rest advance uses claimMagicRounds/runMagicRoundsFor (:953-963); nothing calls decayEnemyAlert. DFU decays the alert in PlayerEntity.Update in every context (PlayerEntity.cs:381-384). The port raises it whenever a foe has the player in sight (:2233) and clears it only when the detecting foe dies (:1847), so underground it only goes up. Its sole consumer is the dungeon resting spawn roll (encounters.js rollDungeon: alert -> 1/36 per rested minute; no alert -> never).
consequence: Resting in a dungeon 8+ hours after last enemy contact (or when the sighting foe was not killed): DFU rolls no interruption spawns; the port rolls 1-in-36 per rested minute forever, breaking long dungeon rests with spawns classic would not mint.

title: Modal RMB mousedown lacks window-up gate: inventory Remove gesture casts readied spell
claim: worldModes' global mousedown (:3402-3404) and mouseup (:3399-3401) feed the modal attack sink on e.button===2 alone. Every sibling gates on a window up: dungeon.js:195 ('a right-click on a window is the window's (the remove gesture), never a swing'), world.js:2062, exterior.js:1168. The sink runs magic.interceptAttack(true) first (dungeonContext.js:1475-1483; interior arm :3391), which latches pendingClickCast when a spell is readied (hostMagic.js:489-492); interior mode fires it the same frame (firePending :2803 runs with the overlay up), dungeon mode fires on window close. DFU windows pause the game on push (UserInterfaceManager.cs:179-185); a window click never reaches the cast.
consequence: With a spell readied, right-clicking an item (Remove gesture) in a modal interior/dungeon inventory or trade window silently casts it - magicka spent, missile fired - where the standalone dungeon and both exterior slots swallow the click.

title: Dungeon fall damage never flashes the screen; the other three hosts do
claim: dungeonContext's own fall arm (reportActivity :2718-2723 - fed by both dungeon hosts, dungeon.js:418 and worldModes.js:2685) does hurtPlayer + FallDamage sound only; its 'ShowPlayerDamage screen flash pends the HUD arc (flagged)' comment is stale - flashPlayerDamage exists and this file calls it for arrows (:1701) and melee (:1945). DFU's ApplyPlayerFallDamage calls RemoveHealth (PlayerHealth.cs:49-58), whose first act is ShowPlayerDamage.Flash() (:36-38), so every damaging fall flashes. shared.applyFallLanding, the arm the other three hosts use (shared.js:531-547), calls flashPlayerDamage for this exact reason; the wave39 test pin covers shared.js and the enemy-blow sites but not this arm.
consequence: A damaging fall in any dungeon (standalone or world-hosted) deals HP with no red damage flash, while the identical fall outdoors or in a building flashes - a per-scene inconsistency DFU does not have.

title: Exterior Detect feeds pass no loot pool though dropped piles and corpses exist above ground
claim: world.js:1180-1183 and exterior.js:586-590 build createDetectFeed with entities only - no loot thunk - while dungeonContext.js:844-848 passes both pools. The HUD comments justify it as 'no loot PILES above ground (FLAGGED)' (world.js:3542-3545, exterior.js:1837-1839), but both hosts mount createDroppedLoot (player drops become world piles, world.js:819 / exterior.js:564) and both have lootable corpse containers (cityGuards/exteriorFoes lootTargets). DFU's PlayerGPS.UpdateNearbyObjects walks EVERY active DaggerfallLoot with no scene gate (PlayerGPS.cs:747, 766-776), so Detect Treasure outdoors marks dropped piles and corpses in DFU.
consequence: Detect Treasure cast outdoors shows no marker even standing over the player's own dropped pile or a guard/foe corpse; the same cast works in a dungeon. The flag's premise ('no loot above ground') has been false since droppedLoot was mounted in both hosts.

title: Painting identity + info macros unported; paintings are purchasable and show raw %-macros
claim: DFU: DaggerfallUnityItem.cs:571 seeds message=Random.Range(0,65536) for Paintings; InitPaintingInfo (DaggerfallUnityItemMCP.cs:42-65) does DFRandom.srand(message), rand()%180 for file/record, GetPaintingRecordPart random_range_inclusive draws, and %sub/%adj/%pp1/%pp2/%an each burn/draw rand() (all five registered in MacroHelper.cs). Port stocks paintings (shopStock.js:61 PawnShop pair 0x0D -> group 13 -> template 284, rarity 3, ~4%/shelf), routes Info to TEXT.RSC 250 (itemInfo.js:79), but expandItemInfo (itemInfo.js:191-204) handles no painting macro, paintings get no message seed, and grep for %sub/%adj/%pp1/%pp2/InitPainting in src/ is empty.
consequence: Buy a painting at a pawn shop, click Info: the panel renders record 250 with unexpanded %sub/%adj/%pp1/%pp2/%an (and likely all variant lines at once, where DFU picks one via DFRandom) instead of the classic generated painting description.

title: StockHouseContainer unported: private house containers are permanently empty
claim: DFU stocks a house container on first access (PlayerActivate.cs:911-913 -> StockHouseContainer): picks an item group from the privatePropertyItems tables by container model + building type, then mints items in a loop with a halving continue chance gated by DFRandom.rand()%100 > continueChance (DaggerfallLoot.cs:369-371) - DaggerfallLoot's only DFRandom draw. The port identifies house containers verbatim (systems/containers.js) but interiorContext.js:127-130 declares private furniture starts EMPTY, worldModes.js:2409-2417 transferAll()s the always-empty c.items, and no port code stocks them; the privatePropertyItems tables do not exist in src/.
consequence: Burgling or exploring any house in the port yields nothing from any container, ever; in DFU/classic the same containers produce the classic private-property loot (clothing, books, weapons, etc.) on first open.

title: Human-enemy gender roll substitutes Math.random for DFU's shared DFRandom draw
claim: DFU decides an unspecified-gender human enemy's gender with the shared LCG: GetTextureArchive does DFRandom.random_range(0,2)==0 -> Male else Female (DaggerfallMobileUnit.cs:626), consuming one shared-stream draw per such enemy. The port rolls the same 50/50 with Math.random at the hosts (dungeonContext.js:924, also :531/:596 via MobileUnit ctor arg, exteriorFoes.js:86), consuming no shared draw.
consequence: One shared-stream draw per unspecified-gender human enemy is skipped vs DFU; DFU's draw rides the unseeded, frame-cadence-dependent stream position (nondeterministic between sessions) and the 50/50 distribution is identical, so no reproducible sequence breaks - negligible observable impact.

title: forceExitToExterior drops the mode overlay without dispose - isResting latches for the session
claim: forceExitToExterior (worldModes.js:3937-3948) nulls interiorOverlay raw and destroys dungeonCtx without disposing its activeOverlay. RestWindow raises entity.isResting on construction (restWindow.js:96, shared.js:1145) and clears it only in _close/dispose (:107-125); DFU always clears via OnPop (:284). Path: rest -> sub-tick runs tickQuests (restSession.js:388-404) -> TeleportPc (actions.js:1818-1819) -> respawnPlayerAtSite (world.js:2386-2395) -> _respawnAtSite (world.js:1549-1550) calls forceExitToExterior synchronously -> the open RestWindow is discarded, setResting(false) never runs. worldModes.js:4007-4012 documents this exact failure class; this door missed the fix.
consequence: After a quest teleport lands mid-rest, playerEntity.isResting stays true until reload: passive fatigue never drains again (worldTick.js:422) and held enchanted items degrade at 60/round instead of 4 (enchantments.js:317) - 15x item destruction, for the rest of the session.

title: Exterior corpse batches never culled, freed, or cleared on teleport - unbounded growth
claim: Both exterior pools keep every corpse forever: exteriorFoes' splice spares corpses (:401), the cull (:286) skips dead foes (:252), and corpseBatches (:60/:214/:486) has no removal path - batches() draws every corpse every frame. cityGuards.js is identical (:95/:290/:445; :248-256 says guards[] cannot be pruned). The teleport core (world.js:1478-1500) never touches either pool. DFU tracks exterior corpse markers as loose objects (GameObjectHelper.cs:839) and destroys them when out of range or on any teleport (CollectLooseObjects :1040-1055; ClearStreamingWorld :993 from InitWorld :584). The port ported that law for player drops (droppedLoot.collectPixel cites :1040-1052) but not for corpses.
consequence: Every kill permanently adds a VAO+buffers and an array entry drawn every frame; corpses from towns you fast-travelled away from still render and probe loot AABBs. GPU memory and draw time grow without bound over a session.

title: dungeonContext.destroy() skips the dead-mark on dropped piles; spawnCorpse lacks a context-alive guard
claim: droppedLoot's async mount guards only on pile.dead (droppedLoot.js:54) and every other removal site sets dead first (:93/:111/:129/:167 - protocol documented at :45-53). dungeonContext.destroy (:3066-3069) frees batches and clears _piles WITHOUT setting dead, so a pile dropped just before exiting whose texture is still warming mints a batch onto an orphan after destroy ran. Same class: spawnCorpse (:1449-1473) awaits getTexture and guards only '!f.dead' (:1459), so a foe killed right before exit mints a corpse batch into the destroyed context's lists.
consequence: One leaked GPU batch per exit-during-texture-warm (drop or first kill of an enemy type immediately before leaving). Rare, but violates the module's own documented ownership protocol.

title: tryEnter's failure path leaks the fully built interior context
claim: tryEnter builds the whole interior context (worldModes.js:2224 - GPU billboard batches plus voxelfolk race meshes) before computing the landing; a null landing throws 'no interior landing' (:2238) before interiorCtx is assigned, and both hosts only log it (world.js:3210, exterior.js:1538 catch -> console.error). Nothing calls ctx.destroy() on that path, so the build's GPU allocations are orphaned. In DFU a failed transition's objects still die with the Unity scene teardown; here the port owns every allocation and the error path drops them.
consequence: A building whose interior yields no enter markers and no doors leaks its full interior GPU allocation on every E-press (repeatable - the door is not marked bad). Reachable only on degenerate interior data I could not confirm exists in the shipped set.

title: audio.ensure guards its await with a boolean - second caller resolves before DAGGER.SND loads
claim: AudioEngine.ensure sets this._booted = true and returns before 'await this.init(fetchBytes)' completes (audio.js:69-88), so a concurrent second caller's await resolves while enabled is still false and its immediate playOneShot/play3d calls silently drop. The sibling MusicService documents and fixed this exact race ('AUDIT 19 F1/F11... The flag is now the PROMISE... A guard set before its own async work is not idempotence, it is a race with a flag on it', music.js:39-54); the sound engine kept the boolean shape.
consequence: One-shots requested between a first ensure starting and DAGGER.SND finishing are lost, not queued. Per-frame callers self-heal (torch loops retry on null handle), so impact today is marginal boot-window sound loss.

title: Exterior quicksave saves no live enemies (encounter foes + city guards)
claim: DFU's SaveData_v1 carries enemyData for every registered live enemy wherever the player stands (BuildSaveData :865, restored :1006), and SerializableStateManager.RestoreEnemyData (:404-425) re-instantiates each one from prefab on load (exterior handled by SerializableEnemy.cs:189-191). The port's worldQuickSave world half (world.js:1635-1641) carries only pixel/native coords/height/piles; exteriorFoes.foes and cityGuards.guards (live spell targets per world.js:1084) are saved nowhere, and worldQuickLoad restores only piles, then sets _lastEncMinutes to suppress spawn catch-up (world.js:1678).
consequence: Quicksave during a wilderness ambush or guard pursuit and quickload: every attacker despawns with no catch-up spawn - a free escape from any exterior fight that DFU's save round-trips intact.

title: Dungeon foe snapshot omits active effect bundles (instancedEffectBundles)
claim: SerializableEnemy saves each enemy's instancedEffectBundles (:120) and restores them via RestoreInstancedBundleSaveData (:222). The port's foes ARE effect targets - applySpellToFoe (hostMagic.js:106-107) runs applySpell on foe.entity and effects.js pushes onto target.activeEffects (:519-547) - but collectWorld's per-foe record (dungeonContext.js:1745-1756) carries only health/dead/feet/yaw/items/hostile/encountered/magicka; f.entity.activeEffects is never snapshotted and applyWorld (:1768-1781) never restores it.
consequence: Paralysis, continuous damage, soul trap marks, and every other timed effect on every dungeon enemy silently ends on quicksave+quickload: a paralyzed boss wakes, a burning foe stops burning - in DFU the bundles survive the load.

title: applyWorld never removes live foes beyond the snapshot; rewound CreateFoe re-spawns duplicates
claim: DFU's load rebuilds the scene and instantiates exactly the saved enemy set (RestoreEnemyData creates one object per saved record; enemies born after the save are gone with the rebuild). The port's applyWorld (dungeonContext.js:1768-1770) patches foes in place by index over w.foes only - a live foes[] entry at an index past the snapshot's length is left standing untouched. Meanwhile restoreSessionState rewinds CreateFoe's spawnCounter/lastSpawnTime (quest/actions.js:1980 saveShape), so the restored action's wave budget no longer accounts for the survivor.
consequence: Quicksave, let a quest wave (create foe) spawn, quickload: the post-save wave stays alive AND the rewound CreateFoe counter spawns it again - duplicate quest foes after a backward load, where DFU's rebuild-from-save yields exactly the saved population.

title: daedraSummonDay/daedraSummonIndex mutated on the entity but never saved or restored
claim: DFU persists PlayerEntity.DaedraSummonDay and DaedraSummonIndex one-for-one (GetSaveData :164-165, RestoreSaveData :332-333). The port stores the coven's remembered daily roll on the same entity - daedraForSummoner mutates state.daedraSummonIndex/state.daedraSummonDay (daedraSummoning.js:109-111) and worldModes.js:1635 passes state: playerEntity - but ENTITY_FIELDS (save.js:30-58) omits both, so snapshotPlayer never writes them and restorePlayer neither restores nor clears them.
consequence: The witch coven's daedra-of-the-day re-derives instead of restoring: reload from a fresh boot and the coven re-rolls (save-scum until the prince you want answers); an in-session backward load keeps the post-save roll instead of the saved one. DFU round-trips the roll exactly.

title: Foe maxHealth (startingHealth) and fatigue not round-tripped
claim: SerializableEnemy saves startingHealth (entity.MaxHealth, :109) and currentFatigue (:111) and restores both (:175 MaxHealth, :177 SetFatigue). The port's collectWorld saves only health/magicka; makeEnemyEntity re-rolls maxHealth with Math.random on every rebuild (characters/enemyEntity.js:80 rollEnemyClassMaxHealth, :85 Range(min,max+1)), and foe fatigue is live drained/restored state (dungeonContext.js:1109-1110 foe sinks) that applyWorld never touches.
consequence: On a rebuild-then-restore load (standalone ?dungeon ?load path) each monster's max HP re-rolls, so restored health can exceed the new max and enemy toughness shifts across a load; on any in-session quickload a fatigue-drained foe keeps its live value instead of the saved one.

title: Interior host cannot save at all (savingPrevented hardwired true)
claim: DFU saves inside buildings: SerializablePlayer stores exteriorDoors + buildingDiscoveryData when IsPlayerInsideBuilding (:183-187) and SaveLoadManager.cs:1410-1418 restores the interior context on load. The port's interior mode wires the pause window with savingPrevented: () => true (worldModes.js:3560; 'You cannot save now.' per pauseWindow.js:192-195) and mounts no quickSave/quickLoad in its routeKey ctx, so F9 inside a building is a silent no-op. Flagged in-code as unbuilt (worldModes.js:3416-3419) - reported so the audit ledger carries the row; refuters should not treat it as an unknown regression.
consequence: A player inside any shop, tavern, temple, or house cannot save the game; DFU saves anywhere. Progress since the last exterior/dungeon save is lost on a crash inside.

title: Weapon drawn/sheathed state not in the envelope
claim: DFU saves data.weaponDrawn (:175) and restores weaponManager.Sheathed = !data.weaponDrawn (:420). The port's sheath state lives on weaponRig.playerWeapon.sheathed in both saving hosts (world.js:892, dungeonContext.js:1482) but snapshotPlayer carries no field for it and neither host's quickLoad touches the rig.
consequence: A save made with the weapon drawn always loads with it in the rig's default state - the player must re-draw after every load; DFU restores the drawn state.

title: Player yaw, pitch, and crouch state not saved with position
claim: PlayerPositionData_v1 carries yaw, pitch, and isCrouching (:212-214), restored by RestorePosition. The port saves only lastPlayerFeet (dungeonContext.js:2729) and restores via setPlayerPos(extras.position) (:2767) - a bare 3-vector; the world host's envelope (world.js:1636) likewise carries coordinates only. The port has crouch (player/motor.js P12) and mouselook yaw/pitch, so the state exists to lose.
consequence: Every load resets facing to the motor default and stands the player up; a save made crouched in a 0.9-height crawlspace loads standing at that spot.
